Coherent Has Massively Diappointed Investors for 6 Months: A Respected Analyst Predicts It Will Double Moving Forward
Coherent keeps beating earnings estimates while its stock slides further from a 52-week high, and now Wall Street's most bullish analyst has a target that implies shares could nearly double from here.
Published October 15, 2026, 8:45am ET · 4 min read
A dynamic stock market screen with an upward trend signifies the optimistic outlook for companies like Applied Optoelectronics, as analysts predict significant gains. © Travis Wolfe / Shutterstock.com
Coherent (NYSE:COHR | COHR Price Prediction) is priced at $263.23, while the average analyst price target sits at $412.52. The difference points to about 56.7% upside.
Coherent makes lasers, optical transceivers and photonic components. Its Datacenter & Communications division now brings in 79% of revenue. With funding from NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), which invested $2B, Coherent also joined the S&P 500 during fiscal 2026.
The gap matters because the business keeps speeding up while the stock goes the other way. With implied upside above 40%, Wall Street is saying the market has mispriced one of the main suppliers of AI connectivity.
Record Quarters and Falling Shares Open a Six-Month Disconnect
Most of the decline came in a single week. Coherent fell 21.32% over the past week, including a 9.22% drop in the latest session. That session came right after a hot inflation report drove the 30-year Treasury yield as high as 5.63%. AI infrastructure names fell, a cloud provider falling 16% and a server maker 11%. Rising rates hit capital-hungry suppliers hardest. Coherent spent $1.103B on capex in fiscal 2026 but generated only $79.5M in operating cash flow.
Over six months, shares are down 15.98%, and the stock trades about 40% below its 52-week high of $440. Optics stocks fell on profit taking with no company news behind it. Earlier, a fiber maker’s $2B at-the-market equity offering dragged Coherent 11% lower in sympathy.
Coherent’s own results stayed strong. Coherent has beaten EPS estimates 4 consecutive times. Its latest quarter delivered non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 versus $1.6171 expected, on revenue up 33.7%.
Rosenblatt’s $500 Target Calls for Shares to Nearly Double
Mike Genovese at Rosenblatt Securities holds the highest target on Wall Street at $500.00 with a Buy rating. That target means 89.9% upside. His thesis rests on three things: an AI transceiver super-cycle, production that is sold out well in advance, and margins that expand as manufacturing scale catches up with demand.
Management’s own comments support that view. “Fiscal 27 is basically completely booked out,” the CEO said. Customer orders reach into calendar 28, and long-term agreements run through the end of the decade. Coherent expects its first quarter above $3 billion in revenue by the end of fiscal 2027. Current-quarter guidance calls for revenue of $2.20B to $2.40B and EPS of $1.85 to $2.05.
Analysts are watching specific catalysts. Indium phosphide output is set to double this quarter, one quarter ahead of plan. Co-packaged optics revenue begins ramping in fiscal Q2. Optical circuit switching targets more than $4 billion of addressable market. Management also keeps its gross margin target above 42%.
Of 24 analysts, 4 have it at Strong Buy, 15 at Buy and 5 at Hold, with zero Sells. Bernstein recently started coverage at Outperform (247 Wall St.). Still, targets are estimates and carry no guarantee. The trailing P/E of 68x against a forward P/E of 30x shows how much of the thesis depends on earnings that have yet to arrive.
Fabrinet Carries the Optics Group’s Deepest Discount
The whole peer group sold off together. Coherent’s decline is a sector event.
Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) fell 19.33% over the past week but remains up 143.18% year to date. At $896.33 against a $1177.34 target, implied upside is 31.4%, which is smaller than Coherent’s. Coverage is heavily bullish, with 5 Strong Buys, 18 Buys and 4 Holds.
Fabrinet (NYSE:FN) dropped 21.09% for the week and is down 13.69% year to date. At $392.93 against a $734.11 target, it shows 86.8% implied upside. Coverage is lighter, with 3 Strong Buys, 4 Buys and 2 Holds among 9 analysts.
Fabrinet carries the largest consensus upside in the group. Coherent sits in the middle, offering a bigger discount than Lumentum with wider coverage than Fabrinet.
Coherent Still Beats the S&P 500 Despite the Slide
At $263.23, Coherent trades well below the $412.52 consensus target, leaving 56.7% implied upside across 24 covering analysts.
The six-month decline of 15.98% hides a strong year. Shares are up 42.62% year to date, while the S&P 500 has gained 12.86%. Over one year, Coherent is up 140.68%.
Coherent’s Booked Backlog Outweighs the Rate Risk
The bullish case improves if Coherent keeps converting its sold-out backlog into revenue on schedule and gross margin keeps climbing toward 42%. The outlook weakens if long-term rates keep rising, the heavy capex keeps burning cash, or hyperscaler spending cools off before co-packaged optics and optical circuit switching reach scale.
A $3 billion quarter and margin expansion would make the consensus target look conservative. On the risk side, Coherent carries about $3.2B of long-term debt and a beta of 2.113, so every move in rates gets amplified.
Contracted demand into calendar 2028 suggests this selloff reflects a rate and sentiment reset. The stock’s high beta points to continued volatility.

Is Coherent (COHR) Using Its AI Capacity Buildout And TSX CDR Listing To Redefine Its Edge?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 3:17 PM CDT 4 min read
Coherent Corp. has recently reported strong AI-driven demand for its optical connectivity portfolio, expanded and sold-out capacity for key data center components into 2029, and ambitious plans to double manufacturing output and indium phosphide capacity over the next year to meet infrastructure needs.
An interesting twist is CIBC's decision to list a Coherent Canadian Depositary Receipt on the TSX, broadening access for Canadian investors just as the company leans heavily into AI data center buildouts and advanced optical networking technologies.
We'll now examine how Coherent's aggressive manufacturing expansion and AI-focused product roadmap may influence the company's existing investment narrative.

To own Coherent today, you have to believe AI data center optics, not its legacy industrial businesses, will drive the story. The near term catalyst is whether sold out capacity into 2029 and the upcoming November earnings update reinforce confidence in that AI backlog. The biggest risk is that heavy capital spending for capacity and PhotonLink ramps fails to translate into sustained cash generation. Recent share volatility after macro and sector selloffs does not materially change that core trade off.
Among recent updates, the PhotonLink integrated optics platform launch stands out. It directly ties into Coherent's AI data center catalyst by targeting 1.6T-class transceivers, co packaged and near packaged optics, and chip to chip links that hyperscalers are testing right now. If customer adoption tracks current interest, PhotonLink could help fill the expanded indium phosphide and module capacity that is already committed into 2029, potentially supporting better utilization and margins if demand holds up.
Yet, against this strong AI demand story, investors should be aware of how rising capital expenditures and capacity commitments could backfire if hyperscaler spending slows or architectures shift...

Applied Optoelectronics Dives 9% as AI Funding Fears Hit Optical Stocks; Coherent Slides 7%, Lumentum Drops 7%
Warnings from two chip giants about AI funding constraints have sent optical networking stocks into a sharp sector-wide slide, and the smallest supplier in the group faces the steepest drop despite record revenue and a CEO forecasting demand that outpaces…
Published October 14, 2026, 12:35pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
The rapid flow of data through fiber optics symbolizes the strong performance and potential for Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) as its stock continues to climb. © Fiber optics lights abstract background (Shutterstock.com) by asharkyu
Optical networking suppliers are sliding again, and Applied Optoelectronics (NASDAQ:AAOI) stock is falling the most as doubts about how artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure gets funded spread through the group. Applied Optoelectronics stock is at $88.99, down 9% in afternoon trading, though it remains up 155% year to date.
Meanwhile, Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR | COHR Price Prediction) stock is at $269.33, down 7% as it follows its smaller peer lower. Likewise, Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) stock is at $920.42, down 7% in step with Coherent. Such a tight range of losses points to a sector-wide revaluation of AI connectivity suppliers.
Thematic funds are feeling the pressure as well, and the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (CBOE:LYTE) is down 8%. Lumentum and Coherent were the fund’s two largest holdings as of August 6, while Applied Optoelectronics carried a far smaller weight in the basket. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 1%, a softer decline that shows how tightly the selling is concentrated in optical names.
Broadcom and Intel Funding Warnings Rattle Optical Names
Optical networking shares began selling off on October 12. The slide came after Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) chief executive Hock Tan stated access to capital could become a bigger constraint on AI expansion than chip shortages. Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) chief executive Lip-Bu Tan also pointed to rising borrowing costs and uncertainty over returns on AI investments. Along with other optical names, Lumentum stock finished among the market’s biggest losers that day.
The selling has continued since, and no company-specific development explains this session’s move in Applied Optoelectronics stock. Applied Optoelectronics completed an at-the-market equity program, raising capital to fund the capacity expansion its optical component business needs. Its completion announcement came on October 5, days before the funding warnings from Broadcom and Intel.
Smallest Supplier Faces the Biggest Capacity Test
Lasers, transceivers and optical components from Applied Optoelectronics, Coherent and Lumentum move data between servers inside AI data centers. Their revenue tracks hyperscale spending. So the group is sensitive to any sign that budgets could tighten (we covered seven non-chipmaker suppliers riding the same AI expansion in a free report here). By far the smallest of the group, Applied Optoelectronics also sells into cable broadband networks, which gives it a revenue base Coherent and Lumentum don’t share.
Record results support the bull case. In Q2 2026, Applied Optoelectronics posted revenue of $191.92 million, up 86.4% year over year, as its datacenter segment more than doubled. The company also returned to adjusted profitability, earning $0.06 per share against a $0.015 estimate.
On the company’s August 6 call, chief executive Thompson Lin stated, “Demand to support next-generation AI infrastructure remains so robust that our near-term revenue is bounded almost entirely by production capacity and key component availability.” Management then guided Q3 2026 revenue to $255 million to $290 million. Lin also forecast that demand would outpace production capacity through mid-2027.
Hyperscale Orders Decide the Expansion Payoff
The open question for Applied Optoelectronics is whether hyperscale customers keep placing orders at the pace its expanded capacity assumes. Its top 10 customers accounted for 99% of Q2 2026 revenue, which leaves little buffer if one large buyer slows down its spending or delays deliveries. Applied Optoelectronics still posted a net loss under generally accepted accounting principles in that quarter, a reminder that its rapid expansion is costly.
Coherent and Lumentum struck a confident tone in August. On an August 12 call, Coherent chief executive Jim Anderson stated, “We continue to see no signs of attenuation in customer demand.” Lumentum chief executive Michael Hurlston added that “data center architects are turning to optical links as a primary means of connectivity,” and the company guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion.
Those remarks came weeks before the funding warnings from Broadcom and Intel, so fresh order commentary from these suppliers could show whether this pullback reflects a real shift in demand. For now, investors may want to keep their exposure to optical names appropriately sized for further volatility.

Coherent Jumps 10% on PhotonLink Push and Bernstein’s Outperform Start; Lumentum Rises 9%, Corning Advances 3%
Coherent's PhotonLink platform and a fresh Wall Street initiation sent optics stocks surging well ahead of the broader market, raising the question of whether this rally signals a durable AI infrastructure trade or another sentiment-driven spike.
Published October 1, 2026, 10:56am ET · 3 min read
Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR | COHR Price Prediction) stock jumped 10% to $315.71 as traders focused on the company’s PhotonLink platform and fresh Wall Street support for AI infrastructure suppliers. Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) stock rose 9% to $1,058.42, while Corning (NYSE:GLW) stock advanced 3% to $158.89.
The broader optics rally outpaced the market. The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (CBOE:LYTE) gained 4% to $25.40, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE ARCA:SPY) slipped 0.2% to $761.11.
Coherent introduced PhotonLink in September as an integrated-optics platform for next-generation AI data centers. The company also expanded its Pluggable Optical Line System portfolio, linking chip-to-chip, inside-the-rack, and high-capacity data-center connectivity products to the same AI infrastructure buildout.
PhotonLink highlights Coherent’s vertically integrated position across materials, lasers, optics, specialty fibers, and related manufacturing capabilities. Coherent said the platform includes more than 10 customer engagements for co-packaged optics and more than 10 customer engagements for near-packaged optics.
AI data centers require more bandwidth and more efficient connections as workloads become larger and more complex. Coherent could benefit if hyperscalers and equipment makers accelerate deployments of advanced optical components, though the company must turn early engagement into sustained orders and profitable production.
Bernstein initiated coverage of Coherent with an Outperform rating as part of broader coverage of U.S. networking and optical companies. Bernstein said networking and optical suppliers could be “structural winners” within AI infrastructure, an assessment that helped reinforce investor interest in Coherent stock.
The research firm also began coverage of Lumentum, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN), and Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) with Outperform ratings. Bernstein initiated Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Corning with Market Perform ratings, providing a more balanced view of an industry that has rallied sharply on AI-related expectations.
Coherent stock’s 10% gain exceeded the 4% move in the LYTE ETF, suggesting that PhotonLink and Bernstein’s favorable initiation gave traders a company-specific reason to bid up the shares. Still, Coherent stock can remain sensitive to shifts in AI capital-spending expectations, customer order timing, and concerns about industry capacity.
Lumentum stock climbed 9% to $1,058.42, extending the recovery that began after a recent optics-sector selloff. Lumentum reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $1.006 billion, up 109.3% year over year, while adjusted earnings per share of $3.23 exceeded the $2.97 consensus estimate.
The company guided for fiscal first-quarter revenue between $1.225 billion and $1.275 billion. Lumentum management said demand signals for 2027 remained “incredibly strong,” while the company also reported that optical-circuit-switch shipments doubled from the fiscal third quarter to the fiscal fourth quarter.
Lumentum could benefit from demand for high-speed networking, optical switching, transceivers, and other hardware needed to connect AI computing systems. Yet Lumentum faces execution risk as the company expands output, with management previously acknowledging that shipments of high-powered lasers were behind demand.
Corning stock rose 3%, a smaller gain than Coherent stock and Lumentum stock but still well ahead of the SPY ETF’s 0.2% decline. Corning supplies specialty glass, fiber, and optical communications products, giving Corning multiple ways to participate in higher data-center connectivity spending.
The LYTE ETF’s 4% advance suggests the market’s buying interest extended beyond a single company. Coherent stock, Lumentum stock, and Corning stock all moved higher as traders returned to a group that benefits from expectations for rising AI network traffic and increasingly demanding data-center architectures.
The Coherent stock rally could continue if AI-related orders, customer commentary, and capital-spending plans remain supportive. However, the same theme creates risk if large customers delay infrastructure spending, if competitors build excess capacity, or if elevated expectations leave less room for execution mistakes.
Coherent has a compelling product catalyst in PhotonLink and a new Outperform rating to support the bullish discussion. Investors should watch for signs that the company’s customer engagements become material revenue opportunities, while keeping position sizes modest because optics stocks can move sharply as sentiment toward the AI trade changes.

GEO Group, Xerox, Jabil, Coherent, and TTM Technologies Stocks Trade Down, What You Need To Know
What Happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after a broad pickup in energy expenses lifted September inflation to 3.7%, surpassing expectations and driving bond yields higher.
The hotter-than-anticipated inflation reading dampened market sentiment across Wall Street, weighing heavily on major benchmark indexes and pulling equities down from recent highs. When inflation accelerates, it often increases expectations that borrowing costs will remain elevated for an extended period to curb economic overheating. Elevated interest rates can compress corporate valuations, particularly across growth sectors such as technology and semiconductors, where future earnings expectations play a central role in pricing.
Semiconductor shares faced extended pressure, marking their seventh consecutive session of declines as market participants recalibrated risk appetites. Beyond higher financing expenses, persistent energy-driven inflation risks squeezing operating margins and weakening broader enterprise spending. Investors are continuing to evaluate whether persistent price pressures will lead to tighter financial conditions and prolonged headwinds for capital-intensive industries.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

The previous big move we wrote about was 13 days ago when the stock gained 10.5% on the news that Bernstein rated the company Outperform with a $350 price target, pointing to optical-module upside as data-center switches move to higher speeds. According to Streetinsider, the firm framed $350 as about 24% upside, valuing the stock at 22× estimated 2028 EPS of $16, and argued optical-module demand should keep expanding with faster networking gear. Bullish AI-infrastructure read-across was reinforced by Citi commentary tagging Coherent as an AI hardware beneficiary, plus investor focus on Coherent's PhotonLink optics platform and AI security demo amid a broader bid in networking names.
Coherent is up 37% since the beginning of the year, but at $266.26 per share, it is still trading 37.6% below its 52-week high of $426.89 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Coherent's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $4,607.

CRDO vs. COHR: Which AI Connectivity Stock Is the Better Buy?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:14 AM CDT 7 min read
Both Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd CRDO and Coherent Corp COHR are beneficiaries of the AI data center buildout, but approach the opportunity from different angles.
Credo specializes in high-speed connectivity solutions, including integrated circuits (ICs), retimers, optical DSPs, Active Electrical Cables (AECs), SerDes chiplets and SerDes IP licensing.
Coherent is a manufacturer of lasers, transceivers, optoelectronic devices and modules, and engineered materials for verticals spanning industrial, instrumentation, communications and electronics markets.
For investors, the choice between CRDO and COHR is not straightforward. Let us break down the fundamentals, valuations, growth outlook and risks for each company to determine which stock stands out.
As AI clusters grow larger, connectivity is emerging as a critical constraint. Management highlighted that the challenge is no longer just bandwidth, but also reliability, power efficiency, signal integrity, telemetry and serviceability. Credo believes its system-level approach, which combines silicon, firmware, manufacturing tests and qualification, remains a key differentiator.
AEC is a system-level product for CRDO and its core growth engine. The company now has deep relationships with five hyperscalers, alongside expanding engagement with Neocloud customers. Credo continues to see higher AEC penetration within existing customers as deployments scale, while the shift toward 200-gig-per-lane 1.6T ports provides another growth opportunity.
The retimer business is another lucrative opportunity. Management noted that the retimer business also delivered record quarterly revenues, supported by scale-up deployments of Screaming Eagle at 100-gig-per-lane and initial contributions from its 200-gig-per-lane Blue Heron retimer.
The most significant shift in Credo's business mix is unfolding in its optical segment. On the last earnings call, management added that it continues to project more than $600 million in optical revenues, with ZeroFlap optics, silicon photonics PICs and optical DSPs each contributing over $100 million. Credo added that its optical DSP business generated "record revenues" in the fiscal first quarter. The company also recognized its first silicon-photonics PIC revenues following the DustPhotonics acquisition, with initial wins involving 800-gig and 1.6T optical transceivers. Credo continues to forecast more than 85% year-over-year revenue growth for fiscal 2027, aided by an expected second-half inflection.
The company's recent product announcements further strengthen its growth prospects. At the October 2026 OCP Global Summit, the company introduced its 1.6T ZeroFlap Active Light Cable ("ALC"). The wide-parallel optical interconnect solution is built for next-generation AI infrastructure, addressing rising reliability and energy-efficiency requirements. The solution targets AI scale-out and front-end networks, strengthening Credo's position in next-generation optical interconnects. Shipments are expected to begin in 2027.
Alongside the new ALC, the company announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics Workstream within the Open Compute Project community. The initiative, backed by a leading hyperscaler and optical technology providers, including AFL, ams OSRAM and BizLink, aims to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem.
The latest developments build on the company's expanding product portfolio. In September 2026, Credo launched its new family of 224G-based ZF optical transceivers. The new products extend Credo's ZF architecture to 1.6T port speeds and combine its 224G-per-lane optical DSP with the Kfir200 silicon photonics-based PICs and latest-generation PILOT diagnostics platform. The products are available in 2xDR4, 2xFR4 and DR8 configurations, supporting a range of AI scale-out interconnect architectures.
CRDO's growth does not come without meaningful risks. In the fiscal first quarter, four customers generated roughly 84% of quarterly revenues. Customer concentration is a major concern as it exposes the company to shifts in customer spending decisions and could materially affect results.
Execution risk is another risk factor. Much of the expected growth in fiscal 2027 is dependent on a successful ramp in the optical business. Any delay in deployment or broader industry transitions could affect this ramp. Macroeconomic uncertainties and exposure to the AI investment cycle amid increasing market competition remain additional concerns. The DustPhotonics acquisition also reduced its cash balance to $764.3 million at the end of the fiscal first quarter.
Explosive growth in AI data center infrastructure is driving unprecedented demand for optical networking solutions, positioning Coherent for long-term growth.
The Datacenter & Communications segment remains Coherent's core engine, contributing 79% of total revenues in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Segment revenues increased 59% year over year, while data center revenues surged 66% on broad-based strength. Growing adoption of 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers bodes well. Management expects the 1.6T transceiver ramp to accelerate in calendar 2026 and 2027 as customer adoption increases.
Coherent expects first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues between $2.2 billion and $2.4 billion, with non-GAAP earnings per share of $1.85-$2.05. The company expects to achieve its first-ever quarter with over $3 billion in revenue by the end of fiscal 2027.
The launch of PhotonLink strengthens its product portfolio. This integrated optics platform combines lasers, silicon photonics, specialty fibers, isolators, specialty fibers, micro-optics and detectors to support co-packaged optics ("CPO"), near-packaged optics ("NPO") and emerging chip-to-chip connectivity. PhotonLink-related revenues are expected to begin ramping in the fourth quarter of calendar 2026.
Beyond transceivers, CPO, multi-rail systems, optical circuit switching ("OCS") and advanced materials for data center, thermal and power management offer additional growth opportunities. OCS revenues increased sequentially in the fiscal fourth quarter, while multi-rail revenues are expected to begin ramping in the first half of calendar 2027. The company expects OCS revenues to improve, supported by capacity expansion, in the upcoming quarters.
On the last earnings call, COHR noted that OCS represented more than $4 billion of addressable opportunity across data center interconnect, scale-up and scale-out networks. Further, management added that CPO, NPO and other forms of integrated optics represent more than $15 billion of incremental addressable opportunity over the coming years as these technologies enable the transition from copper connectivity.
Aggressive capacity expansion strategy bodes well. On the last earnings call, management said that the company was expanding its six-inch indium phosphide production capacity, targeting a doubling of internal output year over year by the end of the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Management expects capacity to more than double again by the end of calendar 2027.
However, the company is witnessing rising operating and capital expenses as it focuses on capacity expansion. While these investments are necessary for long-term growth, they may pressure margins and free cash flow if revenues do not materialize as expected. Capital expenditures reached $556 million in the fiscal fourth quarter, compared with $290 million in the preceding quarter, and management expects further sequential increase in the fiscal first quarter.
Heavy reliance on the Datacenter & Communications segment increases volatility linked to AI spending cycles amid increasing competition and macroeconomic troubles. Weakness in the Industrial segment, owing to softness in broader industrial markets, is concerning.
Price Performance & Valuations of CRDO & COHR
Year to date, CRDO and COHR are up 24.5% and 42.6%, respectively.
CRDO is trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of 23.41X, lower than COHR's 24.73X.
How Do the Consensus Estimates Compare for CRDO & COHR?
Analysts have raised their earnings estimates for COHR by 0.9% for the current fiscal year in the past 60 days.
Estimates have been revised up 4.2% for CRDO's bottom line in the same period.
CRDO offers strong revenue growth prospects but customer concentration and execution risks remain concerns. COHR benefits from a broader optical portfolio, expanding manufacturing capacity and strong AI-driven demand, though rising capital expenditures could pressure cash flow.
COHR carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) while CRDO carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). Coherent appears to be a better pick now based on the Zacks Rank.

Coherent Has Massively Diappointed Investors for 6 Months: A Respected Analyst Predicts It Will Double Moving Forward
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:45 AM CDT 6 min read
COHR fell 21% in one week and sits 40% below its 52-week high, while Wall Street's average target implies 57% upside.
FN and LITE sold off alongside Coherent, but Fabrinet carries the group's deepest discount at 87% implied upside versus Lumentum's 31%.
CEO confirmed fiscal 2027 is completely booked with orders extending into 2028 and a first $3 billion revenue quarter targeted by year-end.
Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Coherent didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat COHR. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.
Coherent (NYSE:COHR) is priced at $263.23, while the average analyst price target sits at $412.52. The difference points to about 56.7% upside.
Coherent makes lasers, optical transceivers and photonic components. Its Datacenter & Communications division now brings in 79% of revenue. With funding from NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), which invested $2B, Coherent also joined the S&P 500 during fiscal 2026.
The gap matters because the business keeps speeding up while the stock goes the other way. With implied upside above 40%, Wall Street is saying the market has mispriced one of the main suppliers of AI connectivity.
Record Quarters and Falling Shares Open a Six-Month Disconnect
Most of the decline came in a single week. Coherent fell 21.32% over the past week, including a 9.22% drop in the latest session. That session came right after a hot inflation report drove the 30-year Treasury yield as high as 5.63%. AI infrastructure names fell, a cloud provider falling 16% and a server maker 11%. Rising rates hit capital-hungry suppliers hardest. Coherent spent $1.103B on capex in fiscal 2026 but generated only $79.5M in operating cash flow.
Why Didn't COHR Make The Top 10 List?
24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
And COHR didn't make the cut!
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.
Over six months, shares are down 15.98%, and the stock trades about 40% below its 52-week high of $440. Optics stocks fell on profit taking with no company news behind it. Earlier, a fiber maker's $2B at-the-market equity offering dragged Coherent 11% lower in sympathy.
Coherent's own results stayed strong. Coherent has beaten EPS estimates 4 consecutive times. Its latest quarter delivered non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 versus $1.6171 expected, on revenue up 33.7%.
Rosenblatt's $500 Target Calls for Shares to Nearly Double
Mike Genovese at Rosenblatt Securities holds the highest target on Wall Street at $500.00 with a Buy rating. That target means 89.9% upside. His thesis rests on three things: an AI transceiver super-cycle, production that is sold out well in advance, and margins that expand as manufacturing scale catches up with demand.
Management's own comments support that view. "Fiscal 27 is basically completely booked out," the CEO said. Customer orders reach into calendar 28, and long-term agreements run through the end of the decade. Coherent expects its first quarter above $3 billion in revenue by the end of fiscal 2027. Current-quarter guidance calls for revenue of $2.20B to $2.40B and EPS of $1.85 to $2.05.
Analysts are watching specific catalysts. Indium phosphide output is set to double this quarter, one quarter ahead of plan. Co-packaged optics revenue begins ramping in fiscal Q2. Optical circuit switching targets more than $4 billion of addressable market. Management also keeps its gross margin target above 42%.
Of 24 analysts, 4 have it at Strong Buy, 15 at Buy and 5 at Hold, with zero Sells. Bernstein recently started coverage at Outperform (247 Wall St.). Still, targets are estimates and carry no guarantee. The trailing P/E of 68x against a forward P/E of 30x shows how much of the thesis depends on earnings that have yet to arrive.
Fabrinet Carries the Optics Group's Deepest Discount
The whole peer group sold off together. Coherent's decline is a sector event.
Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) fell 19.33% over the past week but remains up 143.18% year to date. At $896.33 against a $1177.34 target, implied upside is 31.4%, which is smaller than Coherent's. Coverage is heavily bullish, with 5 Strong Buys, 18 Buys and 4 Holds.
Fabrinet (NYSE:FN) dropped 21.09% for the week and is down 13.69% year to date. At $392.93 against a $734.11 target, it shows 86.8% implied upside. Coverage is lighter, with 3 Strong Buys, 4 Buys and 2 Holds among 9 analysts.
Fabrinet carries the largest consensus upside in the group. Coherent sits in the middle, offering a bigger discount than Lumentum with wider coverage than Fabrinet.
Coherent Still Beats the S&P 500 Despite the Slide
At $263.23, Coherent trades well below the $412.52 consensus target, leaving 56.7% implied upside across 24 covering analysts.
The six-month decline of 15.98% hides a strong year. Shares are up 42.62% year to date, while the S&P 500 has gained 12.86%. Over one year, Coherent is up 140.68%.
Coherent's Booked Backlog Outweighs the Rate Risk
The bullish case improves if Coherent keeps converting its sold-out backlog into revenue on schedule and gross margin keeps climbing toward 42%. The outlook weakens if long-term rates keep rising, the heavy capex keeps burning cash, or hyperscaler spending cools off before co-packaged optics and optical circuit switching reach scale.
A $3 billion quarter and margin expansion would make the consensus target look conservative. On the risk side, Coherent carries about $3.2B of long-term debt and a beta of 2.113, so every move in rates gets amplified.
Contracted demand into calendar 2028 suggests this selloff reflects a rate and sentiment reset. The stock's high beta points to continued volatility.

(“Coherent,” “We,” or the “Company”), a global leader in photonics, announced financial results today for its fiscal fourth quarter and full year fiscal 2026 ended June 30, 2026.

That could be good news for Corning Incorporated (NYSE:GLW), a major manufacturer of fiber-optic cables and connectivity equipment. The company has a supply agreement worth up to $6 billion with Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META).
Corning’s Optical Communications business is already booming. Second-quarter sales jumped 32% to $2.07 billion, while segment net income surged 77% to $438 million.
But CEO Wendell Weeks says higher fiber prices aren’t the main reason.
Why Higher Fiber Prices Aren’t the Whole Story
TrendForce released new research Monday forecasting a global optical fiber shortage of 180 million fiber-kilometers this year, with shortages potentially lasting until 2028.TrendForce puts industry capacity utilization at 92%, while inventories have fallen to just one month’s supply. Expanding production typically takes 18 to 24 months.
As fiber supplies tighten, major customers are signing long-term agreements to secure future deliveries.
Corning’s agreement with Meta runs through 2030 and covers fiber, cables and connectivity products. Meta will also serve as the main customer for an expansion of Corning’s North Carolina cable factory, giving the manufacturer committed demand as it increases production.
During July’s earnings call, Wolfe Research analyst George Notter questioned Weeks about rising prices and the company’s growing reliance on long-term agreements.
“The price is higher, but that really isn’t how we’re driving that profitability improvement,” Weeks said.
Instead, Weeks credited higher-value connectivity products that help customers build networks faster and more cheaply.
Weeks added that Corning could sell more of its newest products if it had the capacity to manufacture them.
Wall Street Remains Bullish Despite Selloff
Corning shares have lost roughly half their value since hitting a record high in June, despite booming demand for its optical products.
UBS raised its price target for Corning to $201 earlier this month, maintaining a Buy rating. Citi is even more bullish, with a $220 target, while Bernstein is more cautious at $140.
On Polymarket, traders put roughly 28% odds on Corning’s third-quarter optical revenue exceeding $2.3 billion, although trading volume is just $3,500.
Meanwhile, a separate Polymarket puts roughly 9% odds on an AI industry downturn meeting the contract’s specific conditions by year-end, with more than $3 million traded on the market.
Meta reports earnings Wednesday, Oct. 21, followed by Corning on Oct. 27.

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.
The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.
Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.
A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.
Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).
How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Corning?
For Corning, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +0.68%.
On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.
So, this combination indicates that Corning will most likely beat the consensus EPS estimate.
Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?
While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.
For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Corning would post earnings of $0.76 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.78, delivering a surprise of +2.63%.
Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times.
An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.
That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. Shares of Corning Inc. (GLW) and Verizon Communications Inc. (VZ) are in focus after research firm TrendForce forecast on Monday that rising artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure demand would leave the global optical fiber market facing a supply shortfall of 180 million fiber-kilometers in 2026.
The firm expects shortages to persist until at least 2028. Separately, it projects spot prices for finished optical fiber products to reach 2.8 to more than five times their 2025 levels in 2026, depending on the fiber type.

According to TrendForce, global optical fiber demand is expected to reach 577 million fiber-kilometers this year, with data centers accounting for roughly 18% to 20% of consumption. That share is projected to climb to 30% to 35% in 2027.
TrendForce said AI data-center demand has tightened global supply since late 2025, with chipmakers and telecom operators joining hyperscale cloud providers in investing in related infrastructure.
Unlike previous telecom infrastructure cycles, the firm said the current shortage reflects sustained additional demand from AI data centers, driving the need for interconnects and high-capacity backbone networks.

Global optical fiber capacity utilization has climbed to 92%, while inventories have fallen from four months in 2024 to just one month. Some leading suppliers are already booked into the first quarter of 2027, while expanding preform capacity typically takes 18 to 24 months.
The pricing impact varies by application. Bend-insensitive fiber used inside data centers is projected to average more than five times its 2025 price, while AI backbone fiber prices are expected to reach approximately 2.8 times their 2025 levels. Mainstream telecom fiber quotations could rise to around 3.7 times their previous levels.
Corning, Verizon Lock In Long-Term Fiber Supply
TrendForce said telecom operators are already shifting from short-term purchases to long-term supply agreements to secure future fiber requirements.

The firm highlighted a September agreement between Corning and Verizon covering approximately 129 million fiber kilometers, or 80 million fiber miles, of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions.
Corning also signed a separate agreement worth more than $3 billion with AT&T (T) in September to supply fiber and cable for its U.S. network expansion.
TrendForce expects such agreements to become increasingly common as AI-related demand continues to grow and manufacturers face lengthy capacity expansion timelines.

Can Meta’s Fiber Partner Corning Capitalize On Rising AI Fiber Prices?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 11:52 AM CDT 3 min read
Prices for specialized optical fiber used inside AI data centers are forecast to average more than five times their 2025 levels this year.
That could be good news for Corning Incorporated (NYSE:GLW), a major manufacturer of fiber-optic cables and connectivity equipment. The company has a supply agreement worth up to $6 billion with Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META).
Corning's Optical Communications business is already booming. Second-quarter sales jumped 32% to $2.07 billion, while segment net income surged 77% to $438 million.
But CEO Wendell Weeks says higher fiber prices aren't the main reason.
Why Higher Fiber Prices Aren't the Whole Story
TrendForce released new research Monday forecasting a global optical fiber shortage of 180 million fiber-kilometers this year, with shortages potentially lasting until 2028.
TrendForce puts industry capacity utilization at 92%, while inventories have fallen to just one month's supply. Expanding production typically takes 18 to 24 months.
As fiber supplies tighten, major customers are signing long-term agreements to secure future deliveries.
Corning's agreement with Meta runs through 2030 and covers fiber, cables and connectivity products. Meta will also serve as the main customer for an expansion of Corning's North Carolina cable factory, giving the manufacturer committed demand as it increases production.
During July's earnings call, Wolfe Research analyst George Notter questioned Weeks about rising prices and the company's growing reliance on long-term agreements.
"The price is higher, but that really isn't how we're driving that profitability improvement," Weeks said.
Instead, Weeks credited higher-value connectivity products that help customers build networks faster and more cheaply.
Weeks added that Corning could sell more of its newest products if it had the capacity to manufacture them.
Wall Street Remains Bullish Despite Selloff
Corning shares have lost roughly half their value since hitting a record high in June, despite booming demand for its optical products.
UBS raised its price target for Corning to $201 earlier this month, maintaining a Buy rating. Citi is even more bullish, with a $220 target, while Bernstein is more cautious at $140.
On Polymarket, traders put roughly 28% odds on Corning's third-quarter optical revenue exceeding $2.3 billion, although trading volume is just $3,500.
Meanwhile, a separate Polymarket puts roughly 9% odds on an AI industry downturn meeting the contract's specific conditions by year-end, with more than $3 million traded on the market.
Meta reports earnings Wednesday, Oct. 21, followed by Corning on Oct. 27.

High-throughput and scalable 3D cell culture systems are becoming a major focus for technology providers seeking to improve research efficiency, reproducibility, and sample utilization. In January 2025, Australia-based Inventia Life Science introduced RASTRUM Allegro, a platform incorporating drop-on-demand bioprinting and precision robotics. The system can generate a 96-well plate in approximately six minutes and a 384-well plate in nine minutes, supporting throughput of more than 35 plates per day.
RASTRUM Allegro delivers post-print intra-plate and inter-plate coefficients of variation below 10%, while downstream assay coefficients of variation remain under 19%. The platform is optimized for patient-derived samples and can produce up to 3.5 times more 3D models from limited cell quantities. These capabilities can reduce the cost per well, improve experimental consistency, and broaden access to sophisticated 3D cell culture workflows for translational research and drug development.
Strategic acquisitions are also reshaping the competitive environment. In December 2024, Germany-based Merck KGaA completed its acquisition of HUB Organoids Holding B.V. for an undisclosed amount. The transaction strengthens Merck's capabilities in organoid and 3D cell culture technologies, supporting its drug discovery operations and the development of next-generation therapeutics. HUB Organoids Holding B.V., based in the Netherlands, specializes in organoid models designed for biomedical research and pharmaceutical applications.
The primary technology categories within the market include scaffold-based systems, scaffold-free systems, and 3D bioreactors. Key applications span cancer research, stem cell research, drug discovery, regenerative medicine, disease modeling, and toxicity testing. End users include biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, research laboratories and institutes, hospitals, and diagnostic centers.
North America was the largest regional market for 3D cell culture technologies in 2025, followed by Western Europe. The global market encompasses Asia-Pacific, South East Asia, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, North America, South America, the Middle East, and Africa. Countries covered include Australia, Brazil, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Japan, Taiwan, Russia, South Korea, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Italy, and Spain.

Corning (GLW) Is Wiring the AI Boom. Can Its Valuation Keep Up?
Corning (NYSE:GLW) delivered the kind of quarter most companies would frame and hang on the wall. Core earnings per share jumped 30% in the second quarter, and management guided to even more growth ahead. The stock's reward, according to CNBC, was a 12% drop after the report, which dragged other optical stocks down with it.
That reaction says more about expectations than about the business. Corning makes specialty glass and ceramics, from the tough cover glass on smartphones to the panels inside TVs. Its biggest unit today sells optical fiber, cable, and connectors. That's the plumbing that moves data between servers inside sprawling data centers, which has rapidly transformed the company's outlook as detailed in recent analysis on Corning's market positioning. So investors are now paying for an artificial intelligence growth story. Whether that price still makes sense depends less on last quarter's beat than on how much of Corning's upgraded long-term plan is already baked into the shares.
Corning Is Moving Beyond Fiber Cables. AI Networking Could Be the Next Big Opportunity
Corning has spent well over a century turning materials science into products other companies design around. That matters here. Once a hyperscaler (a giant cloud operator) builds its network around a fiber and connectivity system, switching suppliers mid-buildout is slow and risky.
The clearest proof arrived in the second quarter. Amazon signed a multiyear, multibillion-dollar agreement for Corning's fiber, cable, and connectivity in its US data centers. NVIDIA struck a long-term partnership to expand Corning's US optical connectivity manufacturing capacity tenfold and its US fiber production capacity by more than 50%. While customers don't commit like that to a commodity vendor, market commentary remains mixed on entry timing after the recent surge, even as Jim Cramer says to wait for Corning (GLW) to fall further before jumping in.
Optical Communications sales climbed 32% to $2.07 billion, while segment net income rose 77%. Enterprise Networks, the part of the unit serving data centers, grew sales 65%. Margins back up the pricing power. Core operating margin reached 20.9%, up 190 basis points (1.9 percentage points), and core gross margin improved to 39.6%. Adjusted free cash flow hit $1.42 billion, against $451 million a year earlier.
Management also upgraded its Springboard plan at its investor day this spring. It now targets an annualized sales run rate of $20 billion by the end of 2026, $30 billion by the end of 2028, and $40 billion by the end of 2030. For the third quarter, Corning guided to core EPS of $0.85 to $0.89, roughly 28% growth. Operational momentum like this highlights why major optical suppliers are catching broader interest, earning a mention alongside component peers featured in 12 High-Flying Stocks to Invest In.
What If AI Is the Only Engine?
The bear case is that Corning's growth is narrower than the headlines suggest. Glass Innovations, which now combines the old Display and Specialty Materials units, grew sales just 1%. Automotive rose 2%, and Life Sciences and Emerging Growth sales fell 15%. Solar sales jumped 90%, yet that segment still posted a small loss.
That ties the stock tightly to data center spending. If hyperscalers slow their buildouts, the business with the fastest growth is also the most exposed, a risk shared by other optical networking stocks like Coherent. The long-term Amazon and NVIDIA commitments soften that blow, but they don't remove it.
Here's where the debate gets sharp. Corning trades at 47.67 times forward earnings, as of October 9. That's well above the sector's 23.23 and its own five-year average of 24.26. Put simply, buyers are paying as if Corning were a very different company from the one that traded in the mid-20s for most of the past five years.
The growth outlook explains much of that premium. Expected EPS growth stands at 33.02% for 2027, and second-quarter core EPS growth of 30% shows the business is already running close to that pace. Yet, despite expanding its market footprint across fiber optics and specialized materials, the company doesn't make the cut among the 10 Best Aggressive Growth Stocks to Buy According to Wall Street Analysts. But a multiple this rich leaves little cushion. The post-earnings slide after a strong quarter shows how fast sentiment can sour when results are merely great. Corning asks you to pay up growth front that's still years away.
Hedge fund interest climbed, with 99 funds holding the stock in the most recent quarter, up from 91 in the prior one. Short interest sits at 2.31% of the float, pointing to relatively limited bearish positioning.
The evidence suggests Corning's moat is widening, as its biggest customers lock in capacity for years. The valuation is the harder sell. At 47.67 times forward earnings, the stock already prices in much of the Springboard plan's ambition.
The setup suits patient, long-term investors who believe AI data center spending has years left to run and who can stomach sharp swings. If you need a margin of safety, it's thin here. Two things would change the picture quickly: a cooling in Optical Communications growth, or a third-quarter result that falls short of guidance when Corning reports later this month.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of GLW as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.
While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.
However, an impressive consensus price target is not the only factor that indicates a potential upside in GLW. Here's What You Should Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. Prices for specialized optical fiber used inside AI data centers are forecast to average more than five times their 2025 levels this year.
That could be good news for Corning Incorporated (NYSE:GLW), a major manufacturer of fiber-optic cables and connectivity equipment. The company has a supply agreement worth up to $6 billion with Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META).
Corning’s Optical Communications business is already booming. Second-quarter sales jumped 32% to $2.07 billion, while segment net income surged 77% to $438 million.
But CEO Wendell Weeks says higher fiber prices aren’t the main reason.
Why Higher Fiber Prices Aren’t the Whole Story
TrendForce released new research Monday forecasting a global optical fiber shortage of 180 million fiber-kilometers this year, with shortages potentially lasting until 2028.TrendForce puts industry capacity utilization at 92%, while inventories have fallen to just one month’s supply. Expanding production typically takes 18 to 24 months.
As fiber supplies tighten, major customers are signing long-term agreements to secure future deliveries.
Corning’s agreement with Meta runs through 2030 and covers fiber, cables and connectivity products. Meta will also serve as the main customer for an expansion of Corning’s North Carolina cable factory, giving the manufacturer committed demand as it increases production.
During July’s earnings call, Wolfe Research analyst George Notter questioned Weeks about rising prices and the company’s growing reliance on long-term agreements.
“The price is higher, but that really isn’t how we’re driving that profitability improvement,” Weeks said.
Instead, Weeks credited higher-value connectivity products that help customers build networks faster and more cheaply.
Weeks added that Corning could sell more of its newest products if it had the capacity to manufacture them.
Wall Street Remains Bullish Despite Selloff
Corning shares have lost roughly half their value since hitting a record high in June, despite booming demand for its optical products.
UBS raised its price target for Corning to $201 earlier this month, maintaining a Buy rating. Citi is even more bullish, with a $220 target, while Bernstein is more cautious at $140.
On Polymarket, traders put roughly 28% odds on Corning’s third-quarter optical revenue exceeding $2.3 billion, although trading volume is just $3,500.
Meanwhile, a separate Polymarket puts roughly 9% odds on an AI industry downturn meeting the contract’s specific conditions by year-end, with more than $3 million traded on the market.
Meta reports earnings Wednesday, Oct. 21, followed by Corning on Oct. 27.

Corning (GLW) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM CDT 4 min read
Wall Street expects a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when Corning (GLW) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.
The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 27. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.
While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.
This specialty glass maker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.88 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +31.3%.
Revenues are expected to be $5 billion, up 17% from the year-ago quarter.
The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.
Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.
Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for GLW
Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.
The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.
Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.
A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.
Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).
How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Corning?
For Corning, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +0.68%.
On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.
So, this combination indicates that Corning will most likely beat the consensus EPS estimate.
Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?
While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.
For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Corning would post earnings of $0.76 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.78, delivering a surprise of +2.63%.
Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times.
An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.
That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.
Corning appears a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

3M Jumps 6% on Expanded Amazon Data Center Deal and Earnings Beat; Coherent Edges Higher, Corning Stays Flat
3M surged past its industrial peers and the broader market on the same day it revealed a complex new Amazon arrangement that ties potential billions in revenue to conditions that have not yet been met.
Published October 20, 2026, 10:58am ET · 3 min read
3M (NYSE:MMM | MMM Price Prediction) stock jumped 6% to $171.91 as investors weighed an expanded Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) data center relationship alongside better-than-expected quarterly earnings. The company also raised its full-year adjusted earnings outlook, giving investors both a near-term profitability catalyst and a longer-term infrastructure opportunity.
The advance outpaced Coherent (NYSE:COHR) stock, which gained 1.33% to $235.11, while Corning (NYSE:GLW) stock was essentially flat, slipping 0.21% to $132.46. Those moves put 3M stock well ahead of the two peers today.
Amazon Agreement Expands the Opportunity
3M expanded its commercial relationship with Amazon to deploy and scale optical connectivity and other data center products. The agreement gives 3M a potential growth opportunity as Amazon invests in infrastructure supporting cloud computing and AI workloads.
As part of the arrangement, 3M issued an Amazon subsidiary a seven-year warrant to purchase up to approximately 3.16 million 3M shares at $164.89 each. About 85% of the warrant shares vest based on Amazon’s purchases of data center products, with that portion fully vesting once cumulative payments reach $6 billion.
The remaining 15% depends on separate milestone conditions, making the arrangement more nuanced than an immediate $6 billion order. For 3M, the commercial upside depends on purchases materializing over time, while an eventual warrant exercise could increase the company’s share count.
3M reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.50 per share, exceeding the $2.39 consensus estimate cited in one earnings analysis. Revenue of approximately $6.6 billion was broadly in line with expectations, making profitability the clearer quarterly surprise.
The company reported adjusted organic sales growth of 3.3%, while GAAP sales increased 1% year over year. Those measures use different reporting bases, so investors shouldn’t confuse underlying adjusted growth with the change in reported revenue.
For the full year, 3M raised adjusted earnings guidance to $9.10 to $9.15 per share, incorporating a new reporting basis. That qualification matters because investors should compare the updated outlook with historical figures prepared on a consistent basis rather than assume the entire change reflects stronger operations.
Coherent stock’s 1.33% gain and Corning stock’s 0.21% decline provided a useful contrast with 3M stock’s 6% jump. The uneven performance suggests investors were responding particularly strongly to 3M’s combination of company-specific developments rather than buying every optics-related stock equally.
The Industrial Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSEARCA:XLI) rose 0.75% to $167.93, offering a broader industrial-sector comparison for 3M stock. Meanwhile, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) gained 0.61% to $771.15.
Against those benchmarks, 3M stock’s advance was substantially stronger than either the industrial group or the broader market. The comparison supports viewing the earnings report and Amazon agreement as important catalysts, although a single session doesn’t establish a lasting performance trend.
3M now has two developments for investors to follow: delivery against the raised earnings outlook and progress converting the Amazon relationship into sales. The company could build confidence if stronger profitability accompanies sustained demand for optical connectivity and other data center products.
However, 3M’s warrant structure ties much of the potential equity participation to future commercial activity rather than revenue already earned. Investors should watch for how purchases develop and whether the resulting growth justifies any eventual dilution.
The takeaway is that 3M stock has both an earnings catalyst and a longer-term growth opportunity supporting the rally. Further gains may depend on execution, so investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest rather than treating the Amazon relationship as guaranteed future revenue.

Investors often choose between specialized materials innovators and broad conglomerates when seeking stability. Are you better off with the focused networking growth of Corning (GLW -0.36%) or the massive scale of Honeywell International (HON +1.59%)?
Corning dominates the market for specialty glass and optical fiber, which are essential for modern communication. Honeywell operates as a multi-industry giant, selling everything from cockpit electronics to warehouse systems. Both companies are adapting to a landscape where efficiency and connectivity define the next generation of industrial expansion.
Corning manufactures highly engineered glass and ceramic products for various global industries. It partners with technology leaders such as Qualcomm (QCOM +1.26%), Amazon (AMZN +0.07%), and Nvidia (NVDA -0.29%) to provide high-density optical interconnects for data centers. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as just two customers account for nearly 28% of optical sales.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $15.6 billion, representing growth of approximately 19.1% compared to the prior year. This increase helped drive net income to roughly $1.6 billion, a significant jump from the $506 million reported in 2024. The expansion in net margin, which measures the percentage of revenue kept as profit, suggests the company is benefiting from higher demand for tech stocks related to networking.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 1.6x, indicating the company has $1.60 in current assets for every $1.00 in current liabilities. The debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.9x, which measures total debt relative to shareholder equity. Free cash flow, which is cash from operations minus capital expenditures, was nearly $1.4 billion for the fiscal year.
Honeywell provides mission-critical automation solutions for industrial markets, refineries, and power grids. The company manages a vast portfolio and recently reached a commercial agreement with Bombardier (BDRBF +4.75%) for avionics and propulsion technologies. Its strategic focus remains on high-growth areas like aerospace and building automation while it divests less profitable units like its warehouse solutions business.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $37.4 billion, reflecting growth of approximately 7.8% over the previous year. Despite the top-line growth, net income fell to roughly $4.7 billion from the nearly $5.7 billion recorded in FY 2024. This resulted in a net margin of approximately 12.6%, which was a decrease from the 16.4% margin seen in the prior twelve-month period.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 2.2x, indicating the company uses a significant amount of borrowed money to fund its operations. The current ratio, which measures a firm's ability to pay short-term obligations, was approximately 1.3x. Free cash flow was strong at nearly $5.4 billion, providing capital for dividends and the integration of new acquisitions.
Corning faces risks from high customer concentration, particularly in its display and optical communications segments. It also deals with global supply chain volatility and the potential for manufacturing interruptions at its 78 worldwide sites. The company is sensitive to currency fluctuations in Asia and Europe while navigating the competitive pressures of the solar sector and intellectual property protection.
Honeywell is currently managing significant litigation risks, including federal securities fraud class actions and matters related to Flexjet. The company also faces operational and cybersecurity risks, evidenced by recent settlements regarding government contracts. Managing a complex global business involves the difficult task of integrating newly acquired entities while divesting units that may impact segment profit.
Honeywell International currently appears cheaper on a price-to-sales basis, while Corning carries a higher multiple that likely reflects its faster recent revenue growth.
Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.
The Forward P/E ratio compares the stock price to future earnings estimates. The P/S ratio measures the stock price against sales over the past twelve months.
Which stock would I buy in 2026?
I'd go with Corning. The transformation this company is going through makes it one of the more interesting industrial stocks to watch right now.
Most investors still think of Corning as a glassmaker, but that picture is changing fast. In Q2 2026, optical communications revenue grew more than 30% year over year as AI data centers continue to demand more connectivity infrastructure. Solar is now a growing business adding meaningful scale. And the company laid out an ambitious plan to grow from roughly $20 billion in annualized revenue today to $40 billion by 2030, a target backed by deepening partnerships with Nvidia and Amazon.
Honeywell Technologies, now a focused automation and building technology company after completing its aerospace spinoff in June 2026, is executing well. Organic sales grew, orders jumped, and the full-year outlook was raised in Q2 2026. For investors who want steady industrial exposure, it is a solid choice.
But Corning is in the middle of something bigger. For investors with a long time horizon, owning a business mid-transformation, before the new story is fully reflected in the stock price, is often where the best long-term returns come from. That's where I'm putting my money.

GLW, VZ, COHR In Focus As AI Fiber Shortage Drives Prices Higher — TrendForce Sees Supply Crunch Through 2028
Global optical fiber demand is projected to reach 577 million fiber-kilometers in 2026, with data centers accounting for a growing share.
single fibers of a fiber optic cable, they enable extremly fast data transfer.(Photo by Oed/ullstein bild via Getty Images)
TrendForce forecasts a global optical fiber supply shortfall of 180 million fiber-kilometers in 2026.
Spot prices for bend-insensitive fiber used inside data centers are projected to average more than five times their 2025 levels.
Expanding optical fiber preform capacity typically takes 18 to 24 months, limiting how quickly manufacturers can respond.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Shares of Corning Inc. (GLW) and Verizon Communications Inc. (VZ) are in focus after research firm TrendForce forecast on Monday that rising artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure demand would leave the global optical fiber market facing a supply shortfall of 180 million fiber-kilometers in 2026.
The firm expects shortages to persist until at least 2028. Separately, it projects spot prices for finished optical fiber products to reach 2.8 to more than five times their 2025 levels in 2026, depending on the fiber type.
ASTS Stock Jumps Overnight: CFO Gets New 3-Year Contract — Here’s What’s In His Pay And Exit Package
Other fiber-related stocks also came into focus, including Coherent (COHR), Ciena (CIEN), and Amphenol (APH), given their exposure to fiber-optic connectivity, optical components and high-capacity networking infrastructure.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
According to TrendForce, global optical fiber demand is expected to reach 577 million fiber-kilometers this year, with data centers accounting for roughly 18% to 20% of consumption. That share is projected to climb to 30% to 35% in 2027.
TrendForce said AI data-center demand has tightened global supply since late 2025, with chipmakers and telecom operators joining hyperscale cloud providers in investing in related infrastructure.
Unlike previous telecom infrastructure cycles, the firm said the current shortage reflects sustained additional demand from AI data centers, driving the need for interconnects and high-capacity backbone networks.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Global optical fiber capacity utilization has climbed to 92%, while inventories have fallen from four months in 2024 to just one month. Some leading suppliers are already booked into the first quarter of 2027, while expanding preform capacity typically takes 18 to 24 months.
The pricing impact varies by application. Bend-insensitive fiber used inside data centers is projected to average more than five times its 2025 price, while AI backbone fiber prices are expected to reach approximately 2.8 times their 2025 levels. Mainstream telecom fiber quotations could rise to around 3.7 times their previous levels.
Corning, Verizon Lock In Long-Term Fiber Supply
TrendForce said telecom operators are already shifting from short-term purchases to long-term supply agreements to secure future fiber requirements.

The firm highlighted a September agreement between Corning and Verizon covering approximately 129 million fiber kilometers, or 80 million fiber miles, of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions.
Corning also signed a separate agreement worth more than $3 billion with AT&T (T) in September to supply fiber and cable for its U.S. network expansion.
TrendForce expects such agreements to become increasingly common as AI-related demand continues to grow and manufacturers face lengthy capacity expansion timelines.
