Meta's Fiber Partner Corning Faces Rising AI Fiber Prices and Supply Shortages
Corning, Meta’s fiber partner, is set to benefit as AI-driven fiber prices are projected to surge over fivefold this year compared to 2025 levels. Corning’s Optical Communications segment posted a 32% revenue jump to $2.07 billion in Q2, with net income soaring 77%. A global fiber shortage of 180 million fiber-kilometers is expected by 2026, with tight supplies through 2028. Corning and Meta have a $6 billion, long-term deal through 2030 for fiber and connectivity products. Despite this, Corning’s shares have fallen nearly 50% from their June high. UBS and Citi raised price targets, while Bernstein warned investors to monitor the fear and greed index closely. Analysts suggest altcoins to watch may outperform as market sentiment shifts.
Prices for specialized optical fiber used inside AI data centers are forecast to average more than five times their 2025 levels this year. Higher prices could benefit Corning Incorporated, a major manufacturer of fiber-optic cables and connectivity equipment. Corning has a supply agreement worth up to $6 billion with Meta Platforms.
Corning's Optical Communications business increased second-quarter sales 32% to $2.07 billion. The business increased segment net income 77% to $438 million. However, CEO Wendell Weeks said higher fiber prices are not the main reason for the profitability improvement.
TrendForce released research Monday forecasting a global optical fiber shortage of 180 million fiber-kilometers this year, with shortages potentially lasting until 2028. TrendForce puts industry capacity utilization at 92%. Optical fiber inventories have fallen to just one month's supply. Production expansion typically takes 18 to 24 months. Major customers are signing long-term agreements to secure future deliveries as fiber supplies tighten.
Corning's agreement with Meta runs through 2030 and covers fiber, cables and connectivity products. Meta will also serve as the main customer for an expansion of Corning's North Carolina cable factory. The commitment gives Corning committed demand as Corning increases production.
Wolfe Research analyst George Notter questioned Weeks during July's earnings call about rising prices and Corning's growing reliance on long-term agreements. Weeks said prices are higher but are not the main driver of improved profitability. Weeks credited higher-value connectivity products that help customers build networks faster and more cheaply. Weeks said Corning could sell more of Corning's newest products if Corning had the capacity to manufacture those products.
Corning shares have lost roughly half their value since reaching a record high in June, despite booming demand for Corning's optical products. UBS raised its Corning price target to $201 earlier this month and maintained a Buy rating. Citi has a $220 price target for Corning. Bernstein has a more cautious $140 price target.
Polymarket traders assign roughly 28% odds to Corning's third-quarter optical revenue exceeding $2.3 billion, although trading volume is just $3,500. A separate Polymarket market assigns roughly 9% odds to an AI industry downturn meeting the contract's specific conditions by year-end. That market has attracted more than $3 million in trading volume.

Prices for specialized optical fiber used inside AI data centers are forecast to average more than five times their 2025 levels this year.
That could be good news for Corning Incorporated (NYSE:GLW), a major manufacturer of fiber-optic cables and connectivity equipment. The company has a supply agreement worth up to $6 billion with Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META).
Corning's Optical Communications business is already booming. Second-quarter sales jumped 32% to $2.07 billion, while segment net income surged 77% to $438 million.
But CEO Wendell Weeks says higher fiber prices aren't the main reason.
Why Higher Fiber Prices Aren't the Whole Story
TrendForce released new research Monday forecasting a global optical fiber shortage of 180 million fiber-kilometers this year, with shortages potentially lasting until 2028.
TrendForce puts industry capacity utilization at 92%, while inventories have fallen to just one month's supply. Expanding production typically takes 18 to 24 months.
As fiber supplies tighten, major customers are signing long-term agreements to secure future deliveries.
Corning's agreement with Meta runs through 2030 and covers fiber, cables and connectivity products. Meta will also serve as the main customer for an expansion of Corning's North Carolina cable factory, giving the manufacturer committed demand as it increases production.
During July's earnings call, Wolfe Research analyst George Notter questioned Weeks about rising prices and the company's growing reliance on long-term agreements.
"The price is higher, but that really isn't how we're driving that profitability improvement," Weeks said.
Instead, Weeks credited higher-value connectivity products that help customers build networks faster and more cheaply.
Weeks added that Corning could sell more of its newest products if it had the capacity to manufacture them.
Wall Street Remains Bullish Despite Selloff
Corning shares have lost roughly half their value since hitting a record high in June, despite booming demand for its optical products.
UBS raised its price target for Corning to $201 earlier this month, maintaining a Buy rating. Citi is even more bullish, with a $220 target, while Bernstein is more cautious at $140.
On Polymarket, traders put roughly 28% odds on Corning's third-quarter optical revenue exceeding $2.3 billion, although trading volume is just $3,500.
Meanwhile, a separate Polymarket puts roughly 9% odds on an AI industry downturn meeting the contract's specific conditions by year-end, with more than $3 million traded on the market.
Meta reports earnings Wednesday, Oct. 21, followed by Corning on Oct. 27.

Corning Incorporated (NYSE:GLW) is one of the top 10 Co-Packaged Optics Stocks to buy in 2026. It is benefiting from the AI data center boom, and its push into photonics could provide another growth driver. On October 12, the company joined Lumentum and Astera Labs to demonstrate optical connectivity for AI rack-scale systems at the 2026 Open Compute Project Global Summit. The demonstration focused on PCIe connectivity over optics, highlighting the industry's push to move optical technology closer to computing hardware.
Earlier, Corning partnered with Nvidia to expand US manufacturing capacity, including a planned tenfold increase in optical connectivity capacity. In my view, these developments show that the company is positioning itself to benefit from both current AI infrastructure demand and the next phase of optical networking. GLW is capitalizing on AI infrastructure demand, but where can investors find other AI stocks that offer an even better growth rate? Corning Is Moving Beyond Fiber Cables. AI Networking Could Be the Next Big Opportunity
Why I Think Corning Deserves a Place on the List
Corning's biggest opportunity is to sell more optical components inside AI systems, not just more fiber-optic cables. During its July earnings call, CEO Wendell Weeks said the company had not traditionally supplied components inside these systems. CPO could change that. Corning already has a growing AI network business, with Optical Communications sales rising 32% year-over-year to $2.07 billion in Q2 2026. Management also said it sees a potential $10 billion revenue opportunity by 2030 from a new photonics platform for components inside equipment. It stressed that the timing and the degree of adoption are uncertain, and it hasn't given a photonics revenue outlook for the next year. In my view, Corning's growing optical networking business gives it an existing growth engine, while CPO could provide an additional source of growth as AI systems become more demanding. Corning's Growth Potential Must Justify Its Premium
Corning trades well above its historical average, and its growth outlook will need to justify that premium. The forward non-GAAP P/E of 44.81x is about 84% above its 5-year average of 24.31x, while the forward price-to-sales ratio of 6.57x is more than double its historical average of 3.14x. Earnings growth could help support these multiples. Analysts expect EPS to grow 30.41% in December 2026 and 33.02% in December 2027. However, slower AI spending or delayed CPO adoption could pressure the stock. In my view, Corning's existing AI networking growth and long-term CPO opportunity make the stock worth buying for investors willing to accept its premium valuation and execution risks.

The global 3D cell culture technologies market is experiencing rapid expansion, supported by growing pharmaceutical research, increased investment in regenerative medicine, and demand for more effective preclinical testing models. By 2030, the 3D cell culture technologies market is forecast to reach $9.8 billion, expanding at a CAGR of 19.9%. Historical growth has been driven by the use of cell culture in vaccine production, increasing cancer research, the limitations of conventional two-dimensional cell models, rising academic research funding, and the expansion of biotechnology research infrastructure.
Future market growth is expected to benefit from advances in 3D bioreactor technologies, improvements in scaffold materials, expanding pharmaceutical drug discovery pipelines, and the rising adoption of personalized medicine. Additional momentum will come from greater use of organoids and spheroids in disease modeling, increased demand for advanced drug-screening platforms, and continued expansion of stem cell and regenerative medicine research. The preference for in vitro models as alternatives to animal testing is also influencing investment and product development across the sector.
Growing demand for organ transplantation is emerging as an important driver of the 3D cell culture technologies market. Rising rates of organ failure, combined with continued improvements in transplantation procedures, are increasing the need for technologies that support tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, organ development research, and preclinical safety evaluation.
Data published by the United Network for Organ Sharing in January 2024 showed that the United States completed a record 46,632 organ transplants during 2023. This surpassed the previous annual record and demonstrated sustained nationwide growth in transplant procedures. As transplant demand continues to exceed organ availability, research organizations are increasingly exploring 3D cell culture platforms for tissue regeneration, toxicity testing, and the development of more predictive biological models.
High-throughput and scalable 3D cell culture systems are becoming a major focus for technology providers seeking to improve research efficiency, reproducibility, and sample utilization. In January 2025, Australia-based Inventia Life Science introduced RASTRUM Allegro, a platform incorporating drop-on-demand bioprinting and precision robotics. The system can generate a 96-well plate in approximately six minutes and a 384-well plate in nine minutes, supporting throughput of more than 35 plates per day.
RASTRUM Allegro delivers post-print intra-plate and inter-plate coefficients of variation below 10%, while downstream assay coefficients of variation remain under 19%. The platform is optimized for patient-derived samples and can produce up to 3.5 times more 3D models from limited cell quantities. These capabilities can reduce the cost per well, improve experimental consistency, and broaden access to sophisticated 3D cell culture workflows for translational research and drug development.
Strategic acquisitions are also reshaping the competitive environment. In December 2024, Germany-based Merck KGaA completed its acquisition of HUB Organoids Holding B.V. for an undisclosed amount. The transaction strengthens Merck's capabilities in organoid and 3D cell culture technologies, supporting its drug discovery operations and the development of next-generation therapeutics. HUB Organoids Holding B.V., based in the Netherlands, specializes in organoid models designed for biomedical research and pharmaceutical applications.
The primary technology categories within the market include scaffold-based systems, scaffold-free systems, and 3D bioreactors. Key applications span cancer research, stem cell research, drug discovery, regenerative medicine, disease modeling, and toxicity testing. End users include biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, research laboratories and institutes, hospitals, and diagnostic centers.
North America was the largest regional market for 3D cell culture technologies in 2025, followed by Western Europe. Corning (GLW) Is Wiring the AI Boom. Can Its Valuation Keep Up?
Corning (NYSE:GLW) delivered the kind of quarter most companies would frame and hang on the wall. Core earnings per share jumped 30% in the second quarter, and management guided to even more growth ahead. The stock's reward, according to CNBC, was a 12% drop after the report, which dragged other optical stocks down with it.
That reaction says more about expectations than about the business. Corning makes specialty glass and ceramics, from the tough cover glass on smartphones to the panels inside TVs. Its biggest unit today sells optical fiber, cable, and connectors. That's the plumbing that moves data between servers inside sprawling data centers, which has rapidly transformed the company's outlook as detailed in recent analysis on Corning's market positioning. So investors are now paying for an artificial intelligence growth story. Whether that price still makes sense depends less on last quarter's beat than on how much of Corning's upgraded long-term plan is already baked into the shares.
Corning Is Moving Beyond Fiber Cables. AI Networking Could Be the Next Big Opportunity
Corning has spent well over a century turning materials science into products other companies design around. That matters here. Once a hyperscaler (a giant cloud operator) builds its network around a fiber and connectivity system, switching suppliers mid-buildout is slow and risky.
The clearest proof arrived in the second quarter. Amazon signed a multiyear, multibillion-dollar agreement for Corning's fiber, cable, and connectivity in its US data centers. NVIDIA struck a long-term partnership to expand Corning's US optical connectivity manufacturing capacity tenfold and its US fiber production capacity by more than 50%. While customers don't commit like that to a commodity vendor, market commentary remains mixed on entry timing after the recent surge, even as Jim Cramer says to wait for Corning (GLW) to fall further before jumping in.
Optical Communications sales climbed 32% to $2.07 billion, while segment net income rose 77%. Enterprise Networks, the part of the unit serving data centers, grew sales 65%. Margins back up the pricing power. Core operating margin reached 20.9%, up 190 basis points (1.9 percentage points), and core gross margin improved to 39.6%. Adjusted free cash flow hit $1.42 billion, against $451 million a year earlier.
Management also upgraded its Springboard plan at its investor day this spring. It now targets an annualized sales run rate of $20 billion by the end of 2026, $30 billion by the end of 2028, and $40 billion by the end of 2030. For the third quarter, Corning guided to core EPS of $0.85 to $0.89, roughly 28% growth. Operational momentum like this highlights why major optical suppliers are catching broader interest, earning a mention alongside component peers featured in 12 High-Flying Stocks to Invest In.
What If AI Is the Only Engine?
The bear case is that Corning's growth is narrower than the headlines suggest. Glass Innovations, which now combines the old Display and Specialty Materials units, grew sales just 1%. Automotive rose 2%, and Life Sciences and Emerging Growth sales fell 15%. Solar sales jumped 90%, yet that segment still posted a small loss.
That ties the stock tightly to data center spending. If hyperscalers slow their buildouts, the business with the fastest growth is also the most exposed, a risk shared by other optical networking stocks like Coherent. The long-term Amazon and NVIDIA commitments soften that blow, but they don't remove it.
Here's where the debate gets sharp. Corning trades at 47.67 times forward earnings, as of October 9. That's well above the sector's 23.23 and its own five-year average of 24.26. Put simply, buyers are paying as if Corning were a very different company from the one that traded in the mid-20s for most of the past five years.
The growth outlook explains much of that premium. Expected EPS growth stands at 33.02% for 2027, and second-quarter core EPS growth of 30% shows the business is already running close to that pace. Yet, despite expanding its market footprint across fiber optics and specialized materials, the company doesn't make the cut among the 10 Best Aggressive Growth Stocks to Buy According to Wall Street Analysts. But a multiple this rich leaves little cushion. The post-earnings slide after a strong quarter shows how fast sentiment can sour when results are merely great. Corning asks you to pay up growth front that's still years away.
Hedge fund interest climbed, with 99 funds holding the stock in the most recent quarter, up from 91 in the prior one. Short interest sits at 2.31% of the float, pointing to relatively limited bearish positioning.
The evidence suggests Corning's moat is widening, as its biggest customers lock in capacity for years. The valuation is the harder sell. At 47.67 times forward earnings, the stock already prices in much of the Springboard plan's ambition.
The setup suits patient, long-term investors who believe AI data center spending has years left to run and who can stomach sharp swings. If you need a margin of safety, it's thin here. Two things would change the picture quickly: a cooling in Optical Communications growth, or a third-quarter result that falls short of guidance when Corning reports later this month.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of GLW as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than GLW and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock.

Can Corning (GLW) Climb 26.12% to Reach the Level Wall Street Analysts Expect?
Shares of Corning (GLW) have gained 2.6% over the past four weeks to close the last trading session at $147.28, but there could still be a solid upside left in the stock if short-term price targets of Wall Street analysts are any indication. Going by the price targets, the mean estimate of $185.75 indicates a potential upside of 26.1%.
The average comprises 16 short-term price targets ranging from a low of $129.00 to a high of $238.00, with a standard deviation of $28.72. While the lowest estimate indicates a decline of 12.4% from the current price level, the most optimistic estimate points to a 61.6% upside. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.
While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.
However, an impressive consensus price target is not the only factor that indicates a potential upside in GLW. This view is strengthened by the agreement among analysts that the company will report better earnings than what they estimated earlier. Though a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't give any idea as to how much the stock could surge, it has proven effective in predicting an upside.
Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for GLW
Here's What You Should Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. And that could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. After all, empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.
For the current year, two estimates have moved higher over the last 30 days compared to no negative revision. As a result, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has increased 0.2%.
Moreover, GLW currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much GLW could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

Here's How Much a $1000 Investment in Analog Devices Made 10 Years Ago Would Be Worth Today
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 6:30 AM CDT 3 min read
How much a stock's price changes over time is a significant driver for most investors. Not only can price performance impact your portfolio, but it can help you compare investment results across sectors and industries as well.
FOMO, or the fear of missing out, also plays a role in investing, particularly with tech giants and popular consumer-facing stocks.
What if you'd invested in Analog Devices (ADI) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to ADI for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?
With that in mind, let's take a look at Analog Devices' main business drivers.
Analog Devices, Inc. is headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts. The company is an original equipment manufacturer of semiconductor devices, specifically analog, mixed signal and digital signal processing (DSP) integrated circuits.The product line is composed of amplifiers and comparators; analog-to-digital converters; digital-to-analog converters; video encoders and decoders; embedded processing products and DSPs; MEMS and temperature sensors; RF/IF components and converters; power and thermal management ICs; and audio/video converters, amplifiers, CODECs, filters and processors.
The company also offers analog, digital and RF switches and multiplexers; analog microcontrollers; clock and timing products; voltage references; interface products such as isolators, translators and transceivers; wireless products and converters; and broadband products including amplifiers, CODECs, chipsets and splitters.
Analog Devices has manufacturing facilities in the United States, Ireland and Southeast Asia. The company also uses outside foundries, mainly Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company for front-end processing, and third-party subcontractors for back-end operations.
The company generated $11.02 billion in revenues in fiscal 2025. It generates revenues from four organized end markets: Industrial, Consumer, Communications and Automotive.
In the Industrial market, which represented 45% of fiscal 2025 revenues, Analog Devices caters to industrial and instrumentation, defense/aerospace, energy management and healthcare sectors.
In the Communications market, which represented 13% of fiscal 2025 revenues, Analog Devices offers products used in internet infrastructure, broadband and wireless applications
In the Automotive market, which represented 30% of fiscal 2025 revenues, the company offers products used in infotainment, electrification, autonomous, ADAS and safety applications.
The Consumer market represented 13% of fiscal 2025 revenues. Analog Devices serves demand for feature-rich, high-performance products such as portable devices and prosumer video/audio equipment.
Putting together a successful investment portfolio takes a combination of research, patience, and a little bit of risk. For Analog Devices, if you bought shares a decade ago, you're likely feeling really good about your investment today.
A $1000 investment made in October 2016 would be worth $6,371.90, or a gain of 537.19%, as of October 19, 2026, according to our calculations. This return excludes dividends but includes price appreciation.
In comparison, the S&P 500's gained 259.10% and the price of gold went up 217.23% over the same time frame.
Going forward, analysts are expecting more upside for ADI.
Analog Devices is benefiting from a broad-based recovery as Industrial demand improves and AI-related data center activity expands across optical and power applications. Long-cycle exposure to automation, test, aerospace and defense, energy systems and vehicle electrification supports durable growth. Sticky design wins and a flexible hybrid manufacturing model help capture demand while keeping channel inventories lean. The completed Empower Semiconductor acquisition deepens ADI's high-density power capabilities for AI infrastructure and expands its content opportunity. Cash generation supports dividends and repurchases. These positives outweigh risks from tariffs and export restrictions, external supply-chain exposure, intense analog competition and higher leverage after the acquisition, although execution remains important.
Over the past four weeks, shares have rallied 5.25%, and there have been 11 higher earnings estimate revisions in the past two months for fiscal 2026 compared to none lower. The consensus estimate has moved up as well.

A company's changing earnings picture is at the core of the Zacks rating. The system tracks the Zacks Consensus Estimate -- the consensus measure of EPS estimates from the sell-side analysts covering the stock -- for the current and following years.
Since a changing earnings picture is a powerful factor influencing near-term stock price movements, the Zacks rating system is very useful for individual investors. They may find it difficult to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts, as these are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time.
As such, the Zacks rating upgrade for Analog Devices is essentially a positive comment on its earnings outlook that could have a favorable impact on its stock price.
Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices
The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, has proven to be strongly correlated with the near-term price movement of its stock. That's partly because of the influence of institutional investors that use earnings and earnings estimates for calculating the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Their transaction of large amounts of shares then leads to price movement for the stock.
Fundamentally speaking, rising earnings estimates and the consequent rating upgrade for Analog Devices imply an improvement in the company's underlying business. Investors should show their appreciation for this improving business trend by pushing the stock higher.

Moët Hennessy, Analog Devices and UC Davis Join Forces to Advance Wine Production Through Breakthrough Chemical Signature Detection Technology Leveraging AI
Researchers have demonstrated the ability to identify the complex chemical signatures emitted from grapes and wine to predict quality risks in wine production faster and more affordably than conventional methods.
TAIPEI, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Moët Hennessy, the wine and spirits division of LVMH, Analog Devices, Inc. (ADI), a global semiconductor leader, and University of California, Davis, a world-renowned leading research university, today announced a groundbreaking joint effort to deploy a new generation of technology aimed at enhancing wine quality and supporting the long-term vitality of vineyards.
Moët Hennessy, Analog Devices and UC Davis Join Forces to Advance Wine Production Through Breakthrough Chemical Signature Detection Technology Leveraging AI
The collaboration builds on a breakthrough technology that has its roots in early research at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Today, ADI continues to advance this technology platform for analyzing chemical signatures across a broad range of applications and, together with teams from Moët Hennessy and UC Davis, is exploring its use in viticulture and winemaking. The joint effort aims to detect and interpret volatile chemical signatures emitted by grapevines, juice, and wine, giving viticulture and winemaking teams much earlier insights into biological processes and potential quality risks.
A world first demonstration: predicting Fresh Mushroom Aroma before it develops
The collaboration's first major achievement addresses one of the wine industry's most complex quality challenges: Fresh Mushroom Aroma (FMA). Researchers at Moët Hennessy's Robert-Jean de Vogüé Research Center have built a unique library of samples and associated data to train machine learning algorithms to recognize the chemical signatures associated with this quality risk.
For the first time, the technology successfully identified samples presenting an elevated risk of developing FMA at an early stage, well before the defect would traditionally be detected. This breakthrough creates entirely new possibilities for proactive quality management, enabling earlier interventions and fundamentally changing how quality risks may be monitored throughout the winemaking process.
Powered by ADI's sensing and machine learning platform, the system analyzes a broad spectrum of chemical information and uses AI to identify which signals matter most, revealing patterns that may otherwise go undetected. Rather than looking only for predefined conditions, the platform continuously learns from complex chemical data, enabling a deeper understanding of biological activity and emerging quality risks.
A technology platform with multiple future applications
Beyond FMA, the organizations view this technology as a scalable platform for living systems analysis, with potential applications wherever biological processes generate meaningful chemical signatures that can be measured, interpreted and acted upon. Additional applications being researched include early detection of vine diseases, soil assessment, and identification of other defects, especially those linked to climate change and related events (e.g., wildfires).
The goal is to support, not replace, human expertise by equipping researchers, viticulturists, and winemakers with decision-support tools for earlier detection and deeper insights. The technology is designed to augment the expertise of growers and winemakers, providing additional information and context while preserving the craftsmanship, experience, and judgment that remain central to exceptional winemaking.
An international collaboration uniting technology, AI and life sciences
The effort combines complementary expertise from:
Moët Hennessy, the world leader in premium and super-premium wines and spirits
ADI, a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge; ADI Health Solutions, ADI's business unit focused on developing AI-driven solutions that contribute to the health of people and the planet
UC Davis, internationally recognized as a global leader in viticulture and enology
Together, the organizations aim to unlock new capabilities for observing, understanding and interpreting the complex grape and wine matrix in support of quality and resilience across the wine industry. Beyond this initial collaboration, ADI intends to make this technology broadly available for future industrial applications, while Moët Hennessy and UC Davis are exploring how shared reference libraries could benefit the wider grape and wine industry.
Manuel Reman, member of the Moët Hennessy Executive Committee, overseeing R&D, and Member of the Comité Champagne: "This breakthrough marks the beginning of a new chapter for viticulture and winemaking. We can rapidly detect and interpret the chemical language of grapes and wine to anticipate quality risks before they become visible. Beyond a technological achievement, this opens an entirely new way of understanding and working, one that will help us produce exceptional wines while building greater resilience for the future."
Max Shulaker, Chief of ADI's Health Solutions Business Unit: "This collaboration unites world-class expertise in cutting-edge AI-enabled sensing systems and viticulture to accomplish something previously impossible: reading the chemical language that living systems emit themselves. By recognizing these signatures before conventional methods can, this technology can help winemakers shift from reacting to quality risks to anticipating them. Our first breakthrough addresses Fresh Mushroom Aroma, but it marks the beginning of a much broader platform for understanding living systems, one that can improve quality and resilience in ways that are just now being explored and unlocked."
Ben Montpetit, Ph.D, UC Davis: "In the face of major global challenges, the continued advancement and resilience of the grape and wine sectors will depend on two things: better knowledge and people equipped to put that knowledge into practice. What is especially powerful about this collaboration is that we are advancing both. We are developing technology that can give viticulturists and winemakers the right information at the right time to make informed decisions, while also training the next generation of experts who will know how to interpret and act on those insights."
About Analog Devices, Inc.
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.

Comprising twenty-five Maisons, internationally recognized for their rich terroirs, the quality of their products, and the artisanal expertise they embody, Moët Hennessy has been committed for many years to an environmental and social program, "Living Soils Living Together."
Established in 1908, UC Davis has continually branched out, challenged the way things are done, and gained recognition for solving complex problems related to health, environment, culture and society. Analog Devices (ADI) vs. TXN and ON: Can AI Infrastructure and Acquisitions Drive Its Next Growth Phase?
Is ADI a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Analog Devices, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. The thesis was published on September 11th, when the stock was trading at $378.78, and ADI gained more than 7% since then. The gain appears to reflect improving earnings expectations, supported by recovering industrial demand and expanding AI data center activity across power and optical applications. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ADI. Analog Devices, Inc.'s share was trading at $405.93 as of October 8th 2026. ADI's trailing and forward P/E were 45.75 and 23.20 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.
This isn't the first time we see a semiconductor company pitched as a great investment. ADI shares gained 80.16% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Texas Instruments Incorporated and Microchip Technology Incorporated gained 67.85% and 25.01%, respectively, during the same period. Why are semiconductor stocks rising so much and is it really a good time to buy them?
Stephen Mandel’s Lone Pine and Whale Rock Piled Into This Little Known AI Stock
In June, we published an article about 12 High Growth Semiconductor Stocks to Buy Now and ADI ranked #5 in that article. ADI returned 2.20% since then. So, hedge funds were right about ADI. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on ADI. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADI) designs and makes analog, mixed-signal, power management, radio-frequency, and digital signal-processing chips used in industries like manufacturing, automobiles, communications, healthcare, and aerospace. Its investment case increasingly rests on two forces working together: a recovery in traditional industrial and automotive chip demand, and rising demand for its chips in artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich
Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential
AI data centers need increasingly complex power delivery, cooling, and signal-processing systems, giving Analog Devices, Inc. a second growth engine beyond its traditional markets. Revenue over the past year came in at $13.9 billion, up a strong 33.7%, with healthy profit margins across the board. The stock trades at a premium to its peer group, meaning investors are betting not just on the current recovery, but on the company sustaining above-average growth and profitability going forward.
The bullish case centers on Analog Devices, Inc. expanding its footprint in industrial and automotive markets while becoming more essential to AI infrastructure (see whether Cadence and Analog Devices could capture more of the smart-vehicle opportunity). As AI computing needs grow, servers require more advanced power and signal-processing components, which benefits the company both from overall AI spending and from selling more chips per system. Its July 2026 acquisition of Empower Semiconductor supports this, aimed at strengthening its power-delivery capabilities for high-density AI systems.
Management followed this in September with an agreement to acquire Alif Semiconductor for $1.35 billion in cash, plus up to $200 million more tied to performance targets, adding power-efficient AI chips for edge devices. (see the opportunities and risks behind ADI's $1.35 billion bet on edge-AI chips)
If AI spending stays strong while industrial and auto demand keeps normalizing, bulls believe this could mean several years of growth rather than a short-term rebound. The company also generated $4.3 billion in free cash flow last fiscal year, giving it $2.3 billion in cash and enough financial flexibility to keep funding acquisitions and investments despite carrying $9.1 billion in total debt.
Wall Street analysts broadly share this optimism. The consensus 12-month price target sits at $470.25, suggesting nearly 29% upside from the current price of $365.07, with individual targets ranging from $365 to $675. Reaching that target would require earnings to grow substantially faster than what analysts currently forecast, meaning the stock's upside case depends heavily on continued strong earnings growth rather than just steady performance.
That said, weaker industrial demand, slower AI spending, or geopolitical disruptions remain key risks. So far, the numbers support the bullish case: gross margin recently climbed to 67.3%, up meaningfully from 62.2% a year earlier, while quarterly cash generated from operations jumped 38% year over year. This suggests the recovery is translating into real profitability, not just higher sales volume. One risk worth watching is that Greater China has historically made up 15% to 20% of revenue, which exposes the company to U.S. export restrictions and competition from China's domestic chipmakers. Combined with its reliance on Taiwan-based manufacturing, this leaves limited room for missteps given how richly the stock is already valued.
Another risk for the stock is failing to win a place in next-generation AI systems. Buying advanced power-delivery technology does not guarantee that customers will choose ADI's chips. Driven by demand for more efficient servers, manufacturers must select components that meet strict performance and reliability requirements. ADI's expanded portfolio still needs to secure those customer approvals. Chip suppliers depend on winning a place in system designs before production begins. Losing those opportunities could limit chip sales per server even while AI investment grows. In our opinion, this risk could pressure ADI's price multiples if its AI capabilities fail to translate into meaningful customer wins.
Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 102 hedge fund portfolios held Analog Devices, Inc. at the end of the second quarter, down from 109 in the previous quarter. This modest pullback suggests institutional investors remain broadly comfortable with the company's margins, recovery, and AI exposure, even as some grow more cautious on valuation. By comparison, Texas Instruments Incorporated (NASDAQ:TXN) was held by 111 hedge funds, up sharply from 71, while Microchip Technology Incorporated (NASDAQ:MCHP) was held by 81 hedge funds, up from 69, and ON Semiconductor Corporation (NASDAQ:ON) was held by 86 hedge funds, up from 58. This divergence suggests institutional investors showed the strongest increase in conviction toward Texas Instruments Incorporated during the quarter, while Microchip Technology Incorporated and ON Semiconductor Corporation also saw meaningful increases in interest, even as enthusiasm for Analog Devices, Inc. cooled slightly despite its strong fundamentals.
Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for the Analog Devices, Inc., with just 1.99% of its float sold short, below Texas Instruments Incorporated at 2.41% and well below Microchip Technology Incorporated at 8.03%. Bearish positioning is also far lower than ON Semiconductor Corporation where short interest stands at 10.43% of float. This suggests that Analog Devices, Inc.'s valuation and geopolitical risks are drawing relatively little outright bearish conviction compared with its peers.
ADI's forward P/E is 23.20x. Texas Instruments Incorporated, Microchip Technology Incorporated, and ON Semiconductor Corporation trade at forward P/Es of 27.55x, 20.53x, and 16.50x, respectively. ADI's own forward P/E was 24.94x on October 31, 2025, putting its current multiple approximately 7% below that level. We believe ADI's premium to Microchip and ON Semiconductor reflects expectations for stronger earnings growth from recovering industrial demand and AI infrastructure spending. However, a lower multiple than last year does not establish that the stock is cheap. Analog Devices, Inc.'s adjusted earnings per share rose from $6.38 in fiscal 2024 to $7.79 in fiscal 2025, an increase of approximately 22%, but remained below the $9.57 earned in fiscal 2022. This shows that earnings recovered in fiscal 2025 after earlier declines, rather than growing consistently over the three-year period. We believe 23.20 times expected earnings could be reasonable if that recovery develops into sustained growth, but the 22% increase alone does not justify its premium. If AI demand helps ADI grow earnings beyond its previous peak, the current valuation could offer a reasonable entry point for long-term investors.
Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Texas Instruments Incorporated (TXN) by The Wolf of Harcourt Street in January 2025, which highlighted analog stabilization, shareholder returns, and manufacturing capacity investments. TXN's stock price has appreciated by approximately 58.57% since our coverage. We believe ADI could be a good long-term investment, as its reasonable valuation offers an attractive entry point if earnings growth continues beyond the cyclical recovery
Analog Devices, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. While ADI offers attractive long-term potential if recovering industrial and automotive demand and expanding AI power-delivery capabilities sustain earnings growth beyond the cyclical rebound, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. Here's How Much a $1000 Investment in Analog Devices Made 10 Years Ago Would Be Worth Today
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 6:30 AM CDT 3 min read
How much a stock's price changes over time is a significant driver for most investors. Not only can price performance impact your portfolio, but it can help you compare investment results across sectors and industries as well.
FOMO, or the fear of missing out, also plays a role in investing, particularly with tech giants and popular consumer-facing stocks.
What if you'd invested in Analog Devices (ADI) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to ADI for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?
With that in mind, let's take a look at Analog Devices' main business drivers.
Analog Devices, Inc. is headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts. The company is an original equipment manufacturer of semiconductor devices, specifically analog, mixed signal and digital signal processing (DSP) integrated circuits.The product line is composed of amplifiers and comparators; analog-to-digital converters; digital-to-analog converters; video encoders and decoders; embedded processing products and DSPs; MEMS and temperature sensors; RF/IF components and converters; power and thermal management ICs; and audio/video converters, amplifiers, CODECs, filters and processors.
The company also offers analog, digital and RF switches and multiplexers; analog microcontrollers; clock and timing products; voltage references; interface products such as isolators, translators and transceivers; wireless products and converters; and broadband products including amplifiers, CODECs, chipsets and splitters.
Analog Devices has manufacturing facilities in the United States, Ireland and Southeast Asia. The company also uses outside foundries, mainly Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company for front-end processing, and third-party subcontractors for back-end operations.
The company generated $11.02 billion in revenues in fiscal 2025. It generates revenues from four organized end markets: Industrial, Consumer, Communications and Automotive.
In the Industrial market, which represented 45% of fiscal 2025 revenues, Analog Devices caters to industrial and instrumentation, defense/aerospace, energy management and healthcare sectors.
In the Communications market, which represented 13% of fiscal 2025 revenues, Analog Devices offers products used in internet infrastructure, broadband and wireless applications
In the Automotive market, which represented 30% of fiscal 2025 revenues, the company offers products used in infotainment, electrification, autonomous, ADAS and safety applications.
The Consumer market represented 13% of fiscal 2025 revenues. Analog Devices serves demand for feature-rich, high-performance products such as portable devices and prosumer video/audio equipment.
Putting together a successful investment portfolio takes a combination of research, patience, and a little bit of risk. For Analog Devices, if you bought shares a decade ago, you're likely feeling really good about your investment today.
A $1000 investment made in October 2016 would be worth $6,371.90, or a gain of 537.19%, as of October 19, 2026, according to our calculations. This return excludes dividends but includes price appreciation.
In comparison, the S&P 500's gained 259.10% and the price of gold went up 217.23% over the same time frame.
Going forward, analysts are expecting more upside for ADI.
Analog Devices is benefiting from a broad-based recovery as Industrial demand improves and AI-related data center activity expands across optical and power applications. Long-cycle exposure to automation, test, aerospace and defense, energy systems and vehicle electrification supports durable growth. Sticky design wins and a flexible hybrid manufacturing model help capture demand while keeping channel inventories lean. The completed Empower Semiconductor acquisition deepens ADI's high-density power capabilities for AI infrastructure and expands its content opportunity. Since a changing earnings picture is a powerful factor influencing near-term stock price movements, the Zacks rating system is very useful for individual investors. Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices
The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, has proven to be strongly correlated with the near-term price movement of its stock. That's partly because of the influence of institutional investors that use earnings and earnings estimates for calculating the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Moët Hennessy, Analog Devices and UC Davis Join Forces to Advance Wine Production Through Breakthrough Chemical Signature Detection Technology Leveraging AI
Researchers have demonstrated the ability to identify the complex chemical signatures emitted from grapes and wine to predict quality risks in wine production faster and more affordably than conventional methods.
TAIPEI, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Moët Hennessy, the wine and spirits division of LVMH, Analog Devices, Inc. (ADI), a global semiconductor leader, and University of California, Davis, a world-renowned leading research university, today announced a groundbreaking joint effort to deploy a new generation of technology aimed at enhancing wine quality and supporting the long-term vitality of vineyards.
Moët Hennessy, Analog Devices and UC Davis Join Forces to Advance Wine Production Through Breakthrough Chemical Signature Detection Technology Leveraging AI
The collaboration builds on a breakthrough technology that has its roots in early research at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Today, ADI continues to advance this technology platform for analyzing chemical signatures across a broad range of applications and, together with teams from Moët Hennessy and UC Davis, is exploring its use in viticulture and winemaking. The joint effort aims to detect and interpret volatile chemical signatures emitted by grapevines, juice, and wine, giving viticulture and winemaking teams much earlier insights into biological processes and potential quality risks.
A world first demonstration: predicting Fresh Mushroom Aroma before it develops
The collaboration's first major achievement addresses one of the wine industry's most complex quality challenges: Fresh Mushroom Aroma (FMA). Researchers at Moët Hennessy's Robert-Jean de Vogüé Research Center have built a unique library of samples and associated data to train machine learning algorithms to recognize the chemical signatures associated with this quality risk.
For the first time, the technology successfully identified samples presenting an elevated risk of developing FMA at an early stage, well before the defect would traditionally be detected. This breakthrough creates entirely new possibilities for proactive quality management, enabling earlier interventions and fundamentally changing how quality risks may be monitored throughout the winemaking process.
Powered by ADI's sensing and machine learning platform, the system analyzes a broad spectrum of chemical information and uses AI to identify which signals matter most, revealing patterns that may otherwise go undetected. Rather than looking only for predefined conditions, the platform continuously learns from complex chemical data, enabling a deeper understanding of biological activity and emerging quality risks.
A technology platform with multiple future applications
Beyond FMA, the organizations view this technology as a scalable platform for living systems analysis, with potential applications wherever biological processes generate meaningful chemical signatures that can be measured, interpreted and acted upon. Additional applications being researched include early detection of vine diseases, soil assessment, and identification of other defects, especially those linked to climate change and related events (e.g., wildfires).
The goal is to support, not replace, human expertise by equipping researchers, viticulturists, and winemakers with decision-support tools for earlier detection and deeper insights. The technology is designed to augment the expertise of growers and winemakers, providing additional information and context while preserving the craftsmanship, experience, and judgment that remain central to exceptional winemaking.
An international collaboration uniting technology, AI and life sciences
The effort combines complementary expertise from:
Moët Hennessy, the world leader in premium and super-premium wines and spirits
ADI, a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge; ADI Health Solutions, ADI's business unit focused on developing AI-driven solutions that contribute to the health of people and the planet
UC Davis, internationally recognized as a global leader in viticulture and enology
Together, the organizations aim to unlock new capabilities for observing, understanding and interpreting the complex grape and wine matrix in support of quality and resilience across the wine industry. Beyond this initial collaboration, ADI intends to make this technology broadly available for future industrial applications, while Moët Hennessy and UC Davis are exploring how shared reference libraries could benefit the wider grape and wine industry.
Manuel Reman, member of the Moët Hennessy Executive Committee, overseeing R&D, and Member of the Comité Champagne: "This breakthrough marks the beginning of a new chapter for viticulture and winemaking. We can rapidly detect and interpret the chemical language of grapes and wine to anticipate quality risks before they become visible. Beyond a technological achievement, this opens an entirely new way of understanding and working, one that will help us produce exceptional wines while building greater resilience for the future."
Max Shulaker, Chief of ADI's Health Solutions Business Unit: "This collaboration unites world-class expertise in cutting-edge AI-enabled sensing systems and viticulture to accomplish something previously impossible: reading the chemical language that living systems emit themselves. By recognizing these signatures before conventional methods can, this technology can help winemakers shift from reacting to quality risks to anticipating them. Our first breakthrough addresses Fresh Mushroom Aroma, but it marks the beginning of a much broader platform for understanding living systems, one that can improve quality and resilience in ways that are just now being explored and unlocked."
Ben Montpetit, Ph.D, UC Davis: "In the face of major global challenges, the continued advancement and resilience of the grape and wine sectors will depend on two things: better knowledge and people equipped to put that knowledge into practice. What is especially powerful about this collaboration is that we are advancing both. We are developing technology that can give viticulturists and winemakers the right information at the right time to make informed decisions, while also training the next generation of experts who will know how to interpret and act on those insights."
About Analog Devices, Inc.
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.
Moët Hennessy is the wines and spirits division of the LVMH group, which also owns renowned vineyards grouped under the "LVMH Vins d'Exceptions" entity. Comprising twenty-five Maisons, internationally recognized for their rich terroirs, the quality of their products, and the artisanal expertise they embody, Moët Hennessy has been committed for many years to an environmental and social program, "Living Soils Living Together."
Established in 1908, UC Davis has continually branched out, challenged the way things are done, and gained recognition for solving complex problems related to health, environment, culture and society. Our 5,300-acre campus borders the city of Davis, a vibrant college town of about 68,000 people. UC Davis is among the most comprehensive campuses in the University of California system, with four colleges and six professional schools that offer over 100 undergraduate majors and more than 100 graduate and professional degrees. UC Davis enrolls about 40,000 students from over 110 countries and contributes at least $13 billion to the California economy each year. In the 2024-25 fiscal year, the university exceeded $1 billion in research funding for the third consecutive year.

ADI's trailing and forward P/E were 45.75 and 23.20 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.
This isn't the first time we see a semiconductor company pitched as a great investment. ADI shares gained 80.16% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Texas Instruments Incorporated and Microchip Technology Incorporated gained 67.85% and 25.01%, respectively, during the same period. Why are semiconductor stocks rising so much and is it really a good time to buy them?
Stephen Mandel’s Lone Pine and Whale Rock Piled Into This Little Known AI Stock
In June, we published an article about 12 High Growth Semiconductor Stocks to Buy Now and ADI ranked #5 in that article. ADI returned 2.20% since then. So, hedge funds were right about ADI. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on ADI. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADI) designs and makes analog, mixed-signal, power management, radio-frequency, and digital signal-processing chips used in industries like manufacturing, automobiles, communications, healthcare, and aerospace. Its investment case increasingly rests on two forces working together: a recovery in traditional industrial and automotive chip demand, and rising demand for its chips in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential
AI data centers need increasingly complex power delivery, cooling, and signal-processing systems, giving Analog Devices, Inc. a second growth engine beyond its traditional markets. Revenue over the past year came in at $13.9 billion, up a strong 33.7%, with healthy profit margins across the board. The stock trades at a premium to its peer group, meaning investors are betting not just on the current recovery, but on the company sustaining above-average growth and profitability going forward.
The bullish case centers on Analog Devices, Inc. expanding its footprint in industrial and automotive markets while becoming more essential to AI infrastructure (see whether Cadence and Analog Devices could capture more of the smart-vehicle opportunity). As AI computing needs grow, servers require more advanced power and signal-processing components, which benefits the company both from overall AI spending and from selling more chips per system. Its July 2026 acquisition of Empower Semiconductor supports this, aimed at strengthening its power-delivery capabilities for high-density AI systems.
Management followed this in September with an agreement to acquire Alif Semiconductor for $1.35 billion in cash, plus up to $200 million more tied to performance targets, adding power-efficient AI chips for edge devices. (see the opportunities and risks behind ADI's $1.35 billion bet on edge-AI chips)
If AI spending stays strong while industrial and auto demand keeps normalizing, bulls believe this could mean several years of growth rather than a short-term rebound. The company also generated $4.3 billion in free cash flow last fiscal year, giving it $2.3 billion in cash and enough financial flexibility to keep funding acquisitions and investments despite carrying $9.1 billion in total debt.
Wall Street analysts broadly share this optimism. The consensus 12-month price target sits at $470.25, suggesting nearly 29% upside from the current price of $365.07, with individual targets ranging from $365 to $675. Reaching that target would require earnings to grow substantially faster than what analysts currently forecast, meaning the stock's upside case depends heavily on continued strong earnings growth rather than just steady performance.
That said, weaker industrial demand, slower AI spending, or geopolitical disruptions remain key risks. So far, the numbers support the bullish case: gross margin recently climbed to 67.3%, up meaningfully from 62.2% a year earlier, while quarterly cash generated from operations jumped 38% year over year. This suggests the recovery is translating into real profitability, not just higher sales volume. One risk worth watching is that Greater China has historically made up 15% to 20% of revenue, which exposes the company to U.S. export restrictions and competition from China's domestic chipmakers. Combined with its reliance on Taiwan-based manufacturing, this leaves limited room for missteps given how richly the stock is already valued.
Another risk for the stock is failing to win a place in next-generation AI systems. Buying advanced power-delivery technology does not guarantee that customers will choose ADI's chips. Driven by demand for more efficient servers, manufacturers must select components that meet strict performance and reliability requirements. ADI's expanded portfolio still needs to secure those customer approvals. Chip suppliers depend on winning a place in system designs before production begins. Losing those opportunities could limit chip sales per server even while AI investment grows. In our opinion, this risk could pressure ADI's price multiples if its AI capabilities fail to translate into meaningful customer wins.
Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 102 hedge fund portfolios held Analog Devices, Inc. at the end of the second quarter, down from 109 in the previous quarter. This modest pullback suggests institutional investors remain broadly comfortable with the company's margins, recovery, and AI exposure, even as some grow more cautious on valuation. By comparison, Texas Instruments Incorporated (NASDAQ:TXN) was held by 111 hedge funds, up sharply from 71, while Microchip Technology Incorporated (NASDAQ:MCHP) was held by 81 hedge funds, up from 69, and ON Semiconductor Corporation (NASDAQ:ON) was held by 86 hedge funds, up from 58. This divergence suggests institutional investors showed the strongest increase in conviction toward Texas Instruments Incorporated during the quarter, while Microchip Technology Incorporated and ON Semiconductor Corporation also saw meaningful increases in interest, even as enthusiasm for Analog Devices, Inc. cooled slightly despite its strong fundamentals.
Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for the Analog Devices, Inc., with just 1.99% of its float sold short, below Texas Instruments Incorporated at 2.41% and well below Microchip Technology Incorporated at 8.03%. Bearish positioning is also far lower than ON Semiconductor Corporation where short interest stands at 10.43% of float. This suggests that Analog Devices, Inc.'s valuation and geopolitical risks are drawing relatively little outright bearish conviction compared with its peers.
ADI's forward P/E is 23.20x. Texas Instruments Incorporated, Microchip Technology Incorporated, and ON Semiconductor Corporation trade at forward P/Es of 27.55x, 20.53x, and 16.50x, respectively. ADI's own forward P/E was 24.94x on October 31, 2025, putting its current multiple approximately 7% below that level. We believe ADI's premium to Microchip and ON Semiconductor reflects expectations for stronger earnings growth from recovering industrial demand and AI infrastructure spending. However, a lower multiple than last year does not establish that the stock is cheap. Analog Devices, Inc.'s adjusted earnings per share rose from $6.38 in fiscal 2024 to $7.79 in fiscal 2025, an increase of approximately 22%, but remained below the $9.57 earned in fiscal 2022. This shows that earnings recovered in fiscal 2025 after earlier declines, rather than growing consistently over the three-year period. We believe 23.20 times expected earnings could be reasonable if that recovery develops into sustained growth, but the 22% increase alone does not justify its premium. If AI demand helps ADI grow earnings beyond its previous peak, the current valuation could offer a reasonable entry point for long-term investors.
Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Texas Instruments Incorporated (TXN) by The Wolf of Harcourt Street in January 2025, which highlighted analog stabilization, shareholder returns, and manufacturing capacity investments. TXN's stock price has appreciated by approximately 58.57% since our coverage. We believe ADI could be a good long-term investment, as its reasonable valuation offers an attractive entry point if earnings growth continues beyond the cyclical recovery
Analog Devices, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. While ADI offers attractive long-term potential if recovering industrial and automotive demand and expanding AI power-delivery capabilities sustain earnings growth beyond the cyclical rebound, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than ADI and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock.

Since October 2021, the S&P 500 has delivered a total return of 76.6%. But one standout stock has doubled the market - over the past five years, Analog Devices has surged 152% to $421.28 per share. Its momentum hasn't stopped as it's also gained 28.7% in the last six months thanks to its solid quarterly results, beating the S&P by 11.1%.
Is it too late to buy ADI? Find out in our full research report, it's free.
Why Does ADI Stock Spark Debate?
Founded by two MIT graduates, Ray Stata and Matthew Lorber in 1965, Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI) is one of the largest providers of high performance analog integrated circuits used mainly in industrial end markets, along with communications, autos, and consumer devices.
Two Positive Attributes:
1. Skyrocketing Revenue Shows Strong Momentum
Examining a company's long-term performance can provide clues about its quality. Any business can put up a good quarter or two, but the best consistently grow over the long haul. Over the last five years, Analog Devices grew its sales at an impressive 16.4% compounded annual growth rate. Its growth beat the average semiconductor company and shows its offerings resonate with customers. Semiconductors are a cyclical industry, and long-term investors should be prepared for periods of high growth followed by periods of revenue contractions.
2. Excellent Free Cash Flow Margin Boosts Reinvestment Potential
If you've followed StockStory for a while, you know we emphasize free cash flow. Why, you ask? We believe that in the end, cash is king, and you can't use accounting profits to pay the bills.
Analog Devices has shown terrific cash profitability, and if sustainable, puts it in an advantageous position to invest in new products, return capital to investors, and consolidate the market during industry downturns. The company's free cash flow margin was among the best in the semiconductor sector, averaging an eye-popping 35.5% over the last two years.
Analog Devices Trailing 12-Month Free Cash Flow Margin
One Reason to Be Careful:
Previous Growth Initiatives Haven't Impressed
Growth gives us insight into a company's long-term potential, but how capital-efficient was that growth? Enter ROIC, a metric showing how much operating profit a company generates relative to the money it has raised (debt and equity).
Although Analog Devices has shown solid fundamentals lately, it historically did a mediocre job investing in profitable growth initiatives. Its five-year average ROIC was 6.5%, somewhat low compared to the best semiconductor companies.

Why Analog Devices (ADI) Is Back In The Spotlight
Analog Devices (ADI) stock is back in focus after fresh analysis highlighted a mix of strong revenue expansion and weaker profitability metrics compared with the broader semiconductor industry, raising questions about how investors should interpret its current valuation.
Recent trading has been strong, with Analog Devices' share price posting a 16.1% one month gain and a 53.6% year to date share price return, while the one year total shareholder return of 82.2% points to momentum that has been building rather than fading.
Compare Analog Devices' surge with a curated group of chipmakers showing similar momentum and fundamentals by scanning our 27 high quality undervalued stocks next.
After a move this sharp in Analog Devices, the real tension is whether buyers are still being paid enough for the extra risk they are taking. It is time to see what the current valuation is really asking you to believe.
Most Popular Narrative: 10.7% Undervalued
On the most followed narrative, Analog Devices screens as undervalued, with a fair value estimate of $470.72 against the latest close at $420.55. This puts the spotlight on what has to go right in the real business for that gap to close.
Further uptake of higher value products and disciplined pricing, underlined by non GAAP gross margin at 72.5% in Q3 2026 with guidance to about 74% and trailing 12 month free cash flow at 36% of revenue, suggests scope for Analog Devices to translate incremental sales into outsized net margin and free cash flow contribution as newer designs ramp.

Still, the Analog Devices narrative could be knocked off course if lower cost rivals pressure pricing in key markets, or if trade restrictions disrupt access to major customers.
Find out about the key risks to this Analog Devices narrative.
Another View: What Multiples Say About Analog Devices
There is a very different message once you shift from that 10.7% undervalued fair value to simple earnings multiples. Analog Devices trades on a P/E of 49.3x, while the broader US Semiconductor group sits at 53.3x and direct peers average a much richer 86.1x.
The fair ratio, which points to where the P/E could move toward over time, sits at 32.7x. That gap suggests the current price already bakes in a lot of optimism and leaves less room for error if growth or margins do not line up with expectations. How comfortable are you paying almost 50x earnings when a 32.7x fair ratio is on the table?

Analog Devices to Acquire Alif Semiconductor, Adding an AI-Native Processing
Platform to Advance Physical Intelligence for the Next Generation of Real-World Systems
Accelerates ADI’s delivery of “Physical Intelligence”, enabling systems to sense, reason, and
act locally in real time within the constraints of the physical world
Adds Alif’s AI-native fusion processors, giving customers a
scalable platform to quickly build full system solutions by combining next-generation digital with ADI’s leading edge analog portfolio
Expands ADI’s total addressable market across industrial, data center infrastructure, defense, energy,
robotics, digital health, and wearable applications by enabling complete, differentiated solutions
Calif., September 9, 2026 – Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) and Alif Semiconductor today announced that they have entered into a definitive agreement under which ADI will acquire Alif in an
all-cash transaction for $1.35 billion.
Artificial intelligence is entering a new phase as models move
beyond interpreting words and images to understanding context and interacting with the physical world. This transition requires systems that can reason from signals such as motion, sound, vibration, radio waves, and thermodynamics, and operate
locally within demanding power, latency, security, and reliability constraints. At ADI, this is called Physical Intelligence.
intelligence with a sophisticated platform of high-efficiency AI-native microcontrollers and fusion processors. Its heterogeneous architecture enables real-time sensor fusion,
low-latency inference, and on-device AI, bringing advanced intelligence to demanding physical systems.
Combining ADI’s leadership in sensing, signal processing, power, connectivity, and application
software with Alif’s leading-edge digital platform will accelerate the delivery of more complete Physical Intelligence solutions. Together, ADI and Alif can address a broader range of customers’ most complex system-level challenges.
“AI is moving out of the data center and into the physical world, where latency, power, and trust cannot be
compromised. That is the domain ADI has mastered for decades, at the delicate electro-physical interface where real-world signals become actionable intelligence. By combining Alif’s digital processing capabilities with our leadership in
multi-modal sensing, signal processing, power, connectivity, and software, we can empower customers to create entirely new classes of secure, intelligent systems that sense, reason, and act locally in real time. This is the next frontier of AI:
embodied and deterministic. This is Physical Intelligence in action,” said Vincent Roche, CEO and Chair of ADI.
“Alif was founded to reimagine what a microcontroller can be in the AI era. We engineered a heterogeneous
architecture from the start, integrating dedicated low-power neural processing with connectivity, security, and intelligent power management that delivers compute resources precisely where they’re
needed. Combined with ADI’s deep physical-domain expertise and broad analog system capabilities, we can expand our reach to deliver the solutions that can power the future of Physical Intelligence,” said Reza Kazerounian, Co-Founder and President of Alif.
Alif’s silicon is already shipping in production, with design
wins across leading consumer and industrial customers.
Under the terms of the agreement, which has been approved by the Boards of Directors of both companies, ADI will pay Alif’s stockholders
$1.35 billion of upfront consideration in cash, subject to the terms of the definitive agreement. In addition, ADI may pay an incremental contingent consideration of up to $200 million. The transaction is expected to close before the end
of calendar year 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and the expiration of the applicable waiting period (and any extension thereof) under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended.
About Analog Devices, Inc.
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:
ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change,
reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today’s innovators stay Ahead of
What’s Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.
Alif Semiconductor, headquartered in Pleasanton, California, is a provider of the next generation of secure, connected, highly power-efficient EdgeAI
microcontrollers and fusion processors. Alif’s architectures scale from single-core to multi-core systems featuring integrated neural processing units (NPUs) and advanced graphics acceleration. Learn more at alifsemi.com.
PJT Partners is acting as financial advisor to
ADI, and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz as legal counsel. Qatalyst Partners is acting as financial advisor, and DLA Piper as legal counsel to Alif.
